Cookies Settings Accept All Cookies', 'The 1960s micro bob is trending! 17 retro haircut ideas and how to style the super short length Search Entertainment Beauty Love and Sex Fashion News and Politics Body Quizzes Lifestyle Work Horoscopes Videos Newsletter Subscribe Win Shop Events Follow Cookies Policy Other Editions Privacy Notice Terms Of Use Skip to Content Celebs Love Beauty Fashion Shopping Body Subscribe Newsletter 8 matte foundations How to wear brown Best protective hairstyles Black Friday Deals London\'s best bars Beauty Hair The 1960s micro bob is trending! 17 retro haircut ideas and how to style the super short length The 1960s micro bob is trending! 17 retro haircut ideas and how to style the super short length Tiny cut, huge impact By Lia Mappoura Updated: 24 November 2025 Ever contemplated, "How short can a bob actually get?" That is, before it enters bixie - pixie territory. Well, prepare to be surprised – because it can go micro short. That\'s right, we\'re talking cheek-grazing, jaw-baring, bone-structure-sculpting short. Move over, cloud bob , layered bob , shaggy bob and co. because we\'re all about the 1960s micro bob revival... A chop so sleek, it\'ll have you wondering if your neck has always been this elegant, the micro bob is not a style for the faint-hearted – the tiny cut is here to make a big statement. But before you go full Twiggy, first, a few questions answered. Specifically: "Will it suit me?" and "How is it best styled?" With the expertise of hairstylist and International Creative Director Mark Hayes of Vidal Sassoon Salon , we\'re here to help you navigate the world of micro bobs. Everyone\'s clicking on... What is a micro bob? As mentioned, the micro bob is not for the faint-hearted, but for those "who love sharp, modern precision," as Mark puts it. It\'s certainly "a power cut," he adds. As for the length, Mark says, "It sits just around the jawline – or even shorter – and is a sleeker, more pared-back version of the classic bob. The edges are typically blunt with minimal layering, which creates a sculpted, high-fashion silhouette." Depending on how it\'s styled, the micro bob is versatile. "It can be worn poker-straight for that glass-like shine, with a soft bend for Parisian ease, or tousled for a cooler, undone look," Mark says. When it comes to its origins, Mark notes that the micro bob is anything but a passing fad – it\'s a true, timeless classic. Of course, many other hair trends have dominated recently (hi, hello Bardot bangs and halo hair ), but we\'re officially crowning the micro bob as the standout style for the 2025/2026 winter season. "It traces back to the daring Flapper era of the 1920s and was catapulted into modern relevance by Vidal Sassoon in the 1960s. He redefined hair with precision cuts that were geometric, bold, and liberating – what we now call the micro bob is a direct evolution of that vision: short, sharp, and endlessly chic." In terms of inspiration, the cut owes as much to design and art as it does to fashion. "Sassoon was heavily influenced by the Bauhaus movement – form follows function," Mark explains. "That philosophy translated into hair through clean lines, minimalism, and timeless structure. You saw it embodied in icons like Louise Brooks in the 20s and later by Mary Quant and Nancy Kwan in the 60s. The micro bob became more than a hairstyle – it became a cultural statement." John Springer Collection // Getty Images Louise Brooks, 1920s Antonia Hille // Getty Images Mary Quant, 1960s Who is a micro bob best suited to? That all said, Mark is clear that the micro bob isn\'t one-size-fits-all. In terms of face shapes and hair types, Mark says, "It flatters oval and heart-shaped faces beautifully and works best on straight to slightly wavy hair, where the blunt line really holds its shape." Unfortunately, Mark explains that "very curly or coarse hair can lose that sharp definition, and rounder face shapes may find it emphasises width. But with expert tailoring, a skilled stylist can adapt the cut to suit a wide range of clients." So, with that in mind, we recommend consulting your hairstylist before committing to the cut! How to style a micro bob While it may look effortless, the micro bob does require some upkeep. "This is a cut that thrives on simplicity but needs attention," Mark says. He recommends using smoothing creams or shine sprays for a polished finish, or a lightweight texturising spray for a more relaxed, lived-in look. "A straightener can also help achieve that iconic Sassoon finish," Mark adds. "But trims every 4–6 weeks are non-negotiable – the cut has to stay sharp to look its best. Think of it like the little black dress of haircuts – minimalist, elegant, and always a statement." Directed by James Cameron , the sci-fi fantasy sequel film once again sees Sam Worthington and Zoe Saldaña reprise their roles as Jake Sully and Neytiri. How much is Avatar 3 expected to make during its opening weekend? Per Deadline , Avatar: Fire and Ash is expected to make $110 million, or somewhere in the $100 million to $130 million range, during its opening weekend at the domestic box office. “It’s behind the first tracking first choice numbers of Avatar: The Way of Water , which opened to $134.1M, and that’s just fine,” the article notes. “Note, unlike most Marvel Studios movies, Avatar movies are appointment viewing. Audiences seek out the best 3D, IMAX, and premium large-format seats. There are no Easter Eggs going on a la a Marvel movie, which require immediate viewing by fans…When we’re talking about the opening for Avatar: Fire and Ash, consider Avatar: Way of Water‘s domestic start essentially the ceiling in regards to a first weekend comp.” The first Avatar movie, meanwhile, made around $77 million during its opening weekend. It ended up making $2.9 billion in total, making it the highest-grossing film of all time. Avatar: The Way of Water, which is the third-highest-grossing movie of all time, finished its box office run at $2.3 billion. As far as 2025 movies go, if Avatar: Fire and Ash makes $110 million opening weekend, this puts it behind the opening weekend for A Minecraft Movie ($162 million), Lilo & Stitch ($146 million), Superman ($125 million), The Fantastic Four: First Steps ($117 million), and Wicked: For Good ($147 million). Jurassic World Rebirth opened on a Wednesday and made $147.8 million over the five-day weekend, though its three-day Friday to Sunday total stands at $92 million. Craft Roundtables ‘Avatar: Fire and Ash’ Casting Director Margery Simkin Talks Importance of Great Actors in VFX-Heavy Work The casting director tells IndieWire, "If you don\'t care about the characters, you\'re not gonna care about the movie," while discussing her work on the visual effects-heavy \'Avatar\' films. By Marcus Jones Plus icon Marcus Jones subject provided Marcus Jones More stories by Marcus ‘Sinners’ Only Needed One Weekend to Remind Everyone It’s a Major Awards Contender Read more Eddie Murphy to Receive AFI Life Achievement Award in 2026 Read more ‘Avatar: Fire and Ash’ Casting Director Margery Simkin Talks Importance of Great Actors in VFX-Heavy Work Read more November 20, 2025 6:00 pm Share Share on Facebook Post google Google Preferred Share on LinkedIn Show more sharing options Share to Flipboard Submit to Reddit Pin it Post to Tumblr Email Print This Page Share on WhatsApp From the outside looking in, the perception around making films like “ Avatar: Fire and Ash ” is that the visual effects come first, and the performances are secondary. But casting director Margery Simkin is happy to clarify that it is actually the other way around when working with Oscar-winning director James Cameron . “The thing that people don’t understand about Jim, because they think about all the technology, is he really cares about the acting and the performances. And he’s a really good director dealing with the actors. And you see it in the auditions,” said Simkin during IndieWire’s recent Crafts Roundtable discussion, presented in partnership with 20th Century Studios. Related Stories Laura Poitras Chased Investigative Journalist Seymour Hersh for 20 Years — and Finally Bagged Him for One of the Year’s Best Docs ‘The Secret Agent’ Review: Wagner Moura Tries to Leave History Behind in Kleber Mendonça Filho’s Beautifully Remembered Period Thriller All three “Avatar” films are a mix of live actors and motion capture performances — mostly those playing the Na’vi tribe of planet Pandora. Though those actors that fall into the latter, like stars Zoe Saldaña, Sam Worthington, and Oona Chaplin, do not have their likeness onscreen, Simkin, Cameron, and company all emphasize that they are providing very nuanced, human performances at the top of their craft. “People think of [Cameron] for all the visual effects, but he really gets that if you don’t care about the characters, you’re not gonna care about the movie. And to care about the characters, you have to have people that are right. So he’s really, really particular and incredibly collaborative,” said Simkin, who has also worked with directors like Tony Scott, Steven Soderbergh, and Guillermo del Toro. All that said, though finding actors for “Avatar” starts as the same any as movie (“You’re looking for great performances, you’re looking for great actors”), the casting director does add that “after we winnow it down, after we get to who we are really interested in having, then there’s the swimming test and all of those kinds of things.” Hence stories of Oscar winner Kate Winslet holding her breath for a record seven-minutes and 15 seconds while working on “Avatar: The Way of Water,” playing a leader of a seafaring Na’vi tribe. “But that stuff can be learned and being right for the part can’t be. So that takes precedent,” said Simkin. Read More: Avatar: Fire and Ash Awards Craft Roundtables Film Margery Simkin Video Daily Headlines Daily Headlines covering Film, TV and more. Disney Park Maps Through the Years "Avatar: Fire and Ash" Movie Theater Collectibles and Novelties Are Ready To Take You to Pandora From Banshee popcorn buckets to themed drinkware, cinemas are bringing Pandora magic to the concession stand. by Reiley Selinger | Nov 17, 2025 2:40pm (Pacific) Tags: Movies , Disney Movies , Avatar , Avatar: Fire and Ash , AMC Theatres , Alamo Drafthouse Cinema , Cinemark Theatres , Regal Cinemas , Popcorn Bucket Avatar: Fire and Ash is bringing its signature wonder straight to movie theaters, and that includes some spectacular food and drink novelties! Tickets for the highly anticipated third installment of James Cameron’s epic franchise went on sale today , and fans can now plan not just their seats but also their themed snacks. AMC Theatres AMC Theatres will also feature a limited number of Banshee popcorn buckets, along with themed cups and toppers, including large drinks, popcorn tins with large popcorn, and a totem cup and lid combo with a large drink. The Adventure Combo bundles two drinks, snacks, and a popcorn. AMC will also serve Avatar-inspired beverages. Cinemark Theaters Cinemark theaters will offer the same Banshee collectible for $79.99, which includes XL popcorn with free same-day refills. Additional options include a 44 oz cup for $7.75, a 20 oz tumbler for $17.95, and a 130 oz popcorn tin for $15, all with same-day refills. Regal Cinemas Regal Cinemas is introducing the Banshee Popcorn Collectible, designed to resemble the iconic blue-winged ikran. The bucket features a faux woven basket on the Banshee’s back filled with popcorn, available at select locations while supplies last. Regal has not announced pricing for this item. Alamo Drafthouse Alamo Drafthouse fans can pre-order a limited edition 16 oz Avatar: Fire and Ash pint glass with their tickets, available for pickup within 30 days of their showtime. About Avatar: Fire and Ash : Avatar: Fire and Ash premieres in theaters on December 19, 2025, but the excitement begins early with the Avatar: Fire and Ash premiere tour kicking off on December 1 at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood. The third installment continues the story of Pandora, written by James Cameron, Rick Jaffa, and Amanda Silver. The star-studded cast includes Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Sigourney Weaver, Stephen Lang, Oona Chaplin, Cliff Curtis, Britain Dalton, Trinity Bliss, Jack Champion, Bailey Bass, Kate Winslet, David Thewlis, and Michelle Yeoh. Plus, Miley Cyrus has recorded an original song for the film. All Rights Reserved Denzel Washington And Russell Crowe\'s Mind-Bending Sci-Fi Movie Deserves Another Look NEWS MOVIES TV TRAILERS REVIEWS EXCLUSIVES FEATURES Newsletter Movies Science Fiction Movies Denzel Washington And Russell Crowe\'s Mind-Bending Sci-Fi Movie Deserves Another Look By Witney Seibold Nov. 11, 2025 12:20 pm EST Paramount The premise for Brett Leonard\'s 1995 sci-fi cop thriller "Virtuosity" is B-movie gold. Denzel Washington plays Parker Barnes, an ex-cop who is currently in prison for murdering a suspect. The suspect in question was a serial killer named Matthew Grimes, who was fleeing after having freshly murdered Parker\'s wife and child, so one can understand why he was moved to a murderous rage. In the chase, however, Parker also accidentally shot and killed two onlookers, so he was sentenced to life in prison. "Virtuosity" is set in the near future, and the Department of Corrections has enlisted prisoners to test a new kind of police-training technology. Trainees are put into a complex Virtual Reality setup and asked to virtually hunt the world\'s most dangerous criminal. If the trainees can capture the video criminal, the thinking goes, they\'ll be ready to slap the criminal element around for real. As a former cop, Parker is the ideal test subject for the tech. The fun twist: the ultra-dangerous V.R. criminal is SID 6.7, a specialized program that was extrapolated from the minds, habits, and pathologies of all the most notorious criminals in history (Manson! Gacy! And the rest!). S.I.D. stands for (snicker) Sadistic, Intelligent, and Dangerous. Sid is played by Russell Crowe, and he savors playing such a cartoonishly evil character. Naturally, Sid has outgrown his programming, has achieved consciousness, and longs to somehow break out of the computer and commit acts of mayhem in the real world. Luckily for Sid, an errant cyberneticist named Clyde (Kevin J. O\'Connor) has been developing a new kind of liquid android technology that can take personality programs like Sid and insert them into hastily grown android bodies. No points for guessing Sid will become a killer android in short order. This movie is awesome. Virtuosity is glorious B-movie fun Paramount The Clyde character, it should be noted, is duped into creating the Sid 6.7 android by his boss (Stephen Spinella). Clyde thinks he\'s growing an android of his ideal virtual girlfriend, Sheila 3.2 (Heidi Schanz). The androids in the world of "Virtuosity" aren\'t so much machines as they are living masses of computerized liquid. When Sid 6.7 gets injured or loses a body part, people can see the bright blue glop on the inside. Sid can reach out toward panes of glass and absorb the glass molecules to rebuild himself. Once Sid is out in the real world, he becomes the sexiest man alive, dressing in slim-fitting, brightly colored suits and strolling through the public with the utmost confidence. Because he is made of every serial killer alive, he looks for whatever opportunities he can to torture and murder. Naturally, because Parker was trained on the virtual version of Sid 6.7, he is released from prison to hunt down the real one. He is paired with a crime psychologist played by Kelly Lynch, and they have to track Sid\'s movements and predict his crimes. A young Kaley Cuoco plays the Lynch character\'s daughter, and the cast is stacked with notable character actors. Bill Forsythe plays the police chief, and Oscar-winner Louise Fletcher plays the Commissioner. Costa Mandylor from the "Saw" sequels plays a fellow prisoner, and Traci Lords has a cameo appearance as a club singer. The soundtrack was full of bangers by artists like Peter Gabriel, Live, and The Heads (the David Byrne-free lineup of the Talking Heads). There is an awesome scene wherein Sid strolls down the street to the Bee-Gees\' "Stayin\' Alive," the best use of that song outside of "Airplane!" Critics hated Virtuosity Paramount Brett Leonard was selected to direct "Virtuosity" because he had a hit a few years earlier with the V.R.-themed horror film "The Lawnmower Man" (the one Stephen King sued to have his name removed from). The story goes that the original script was so bad that Denzel Washington improvised new lines to give the story new details. Notably, Washington removed a romance that was meant to blossom between him and the Lynch character. Critics weren\'t fond of "Virtuosity," and the film only has a 31% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes (based on 36 reviews). Mick LaSalle from the San Francisco Chronicle noted that Washington was the only good thing about it, and Peter Travers of Rolling Stone felt that the action was bland and uninvolving. Hal Hinson in the Washington Post felt that the film had no new ideas, recycling a lot of old sci-fi tropes to muted effect. Roger Ebert was a rare outlier in that he gave the film three stars, feeling that the sci-fi ideas were intriguing. He wrote that "The movie is filled with bright ideas and fresh thinking, but the underlying story is as old as the hills, right down to a final confrontation on catwalks." "Virtuosity" was a financial disappointment, however, making only $37 million on its $30 million budget. A pity because the film is wildly fun. It\'s bright, brisk, and sports two marvelous lead performances. Crowe, usually operating at the height of his powers , is particularly notable here. If an actor can play subtle and subdued dramatic characters as well as broad, cartoonish villains, it\'s proof of their talents. Crowe and Washington would reunite to swap their cop/criminal roles in Ridley Scott\'s 2007 biography "American Gangster." It\'s good, but it\'s not as good as "Virtuosity." Recommended']

news_text_raw: ["Nearly 100 Brazilian students find their fit at UNI | inside UNI Skip to main content Breadcrumb UNI Home inside UNI Campus & Community Nearly 100 Brazilian Students Find Their Fit At UNI Search all news insideUNI ☰ Explore Topics All Stories & News Arts & Design Announcements Alumni Business Campus & Community Education Environment Health Human & Social Services Languages & Communications Newsroom Politics & Justice Pre-Professional STEM Nearly 100 Brazilian students find their fit at UNI Nearly 100 Brazilian students find their fit at UNI Anna Flanders / Nov 17, 2025 When a Brazilian education agency came to Iowa looking for a host university for nearly 100 high school students, UNI was an easy choice. UNI offers a Culture & Intensive English Program (CIEP) to help students improve their English language skills, something that is rare these days among institutions in Iowa. UNI had available on-campus housing, another challenge to find elsewhere for so many students. And, just as many UNI students describe, the campus just felt right. “They said they didn’t want to keep looking,” Carolina Coronado-Park said about the agency when they toured UNI. “They knew UNI was the best place for their students.” The first 50 students are already in Cedar Falls. Their presence is part of a growing partnership between the State of Iowa and the government of Paraná, a Brazilian state. Several Paraná state representatives came to Iowa last April to tour some of the state’s universities and community colleges at the invitation of Gov. Kim Reynolds. This visit planted the seed that UNI could be a temporary home to the group of Brazilian high schoolers. “We're trying to do our best to keep working and connecting with Paraná, not only with the educational agency to bring high schoolers, but also connecting with universities,” Coronado-Park explained. “We're trying to see if we can develop more connections statewide.” The visitors are a group of high-achieving students who are using this opportunity to not only better their English skills but also learn more about agribusiness and entrepreneurship. The CIEP has customized its curriculum around these topics and partnered with the UNI John Pappajohn Entrepreneurial Center (JPEC) to provide the best education possible and meet the requirements set forth by the Paraná government. Because agriculture in Iowa is very similar to their home state, the things the students are learning are very applicable if they choose to remain there after high school graduation. The first eight weeks of the CIEP course focused on agribusiness. On campus, the students explored a variety of topics before going out into the community and traveling throughout Iowa to see agricultural opportunities at Hansen’s Dairy Farm, John Deere, Corteva Agriscience, and more. “When the students came here, at first, they were a little bit shy and not that engaged in the classroom, but gradually they started getting more engaged and understanding basic instructions,” said Moussa Barry, an English language program specialist for the CIEP who has been teaching the students. “Now, they understand all the instructions. They engage in all of the activities we do in class.” \u200c The second half of the semester focuses on entrepreneurship. These classes are led by Reyna Jorgenson, a two-time Wilson College of Business alum whose upcycling business is housed in the JPEC. “I have watched the students become more curious and engaged as they take in the new perspective,” said Jorgenson. “Getting to expose the students to Iowa's entrepreneurial community while also personally getting to learn about Brazil has been a meaningful and memorable experience for me.” In addition to business tours, the students have had other exciting opportunities, including their participation in the Norman Borlaug International Dialogue in Des Moines, where they met the 2025 World Food Prize Laureate Mariangela Hungria, who is also from Paraná. “That sparked a lot of motivation and inspiration for them,” said Barry. With just a few weeks left of their experience, the students are already reflecting on all they’ve learned and gained from their time at UNI. “My experience here has been incredible,” said Anthony Francisco De Olivera. “I have improved my English to a level I never imagined reaching before.” “I will miss the environment you guys have here, the friends I made here, and everything, because it's a really good memory I have from here, from this space, from just college, and I think it's a really nice place,” said Eliza Hilda Schneider. In the spring, 47 more students will come to UNI to go through the same program. Coronado-Park will also travel to Paraná in January with the Iowa Economic Development Authority representatives to connect with business, research centers, universities and local government. One of the goals is to explore the possibility of dual degree programs. Not only are opportunities like these beneficial for international students, but they are also beneficial to UNI students from the United States. \u200c “Bringing students here and helping them connect with domestic students allows us to make the world more accessible to everyone,” said Coronado-Park. “That is our vision: to continue welcoming international students to our campus and to keep inspiring our students, faculty, and staff to explore the world through research, cultural engagement, and knowledge-exchange opportunities. Thinking globally offers a more humble, informed perspective of the academic world. Author of the article: Jacob Robinson Published Nov 26, 2025 • Last updated 1 day ago • 3 minute read Join the conversation Norfolk County filmmaker Dean Rainey is set to present the newest edition of his Building History series. The latest films include one on Deltasia, an amusement park built on the outskirts of town in the 1960s. Photo by Rainey Media Article content In looking to bring history to life for newcomers to Norfolk County, local filmmaker and producer Dean Rainey made a shocking discovery. Article content Alongside his brother Daryl of Progressive Realty Group along with help from Norfolk County Heritage and Culture, the duo has created four seasons of Building History – each focusing on historic buildings in local towns. Play Video Article content “With so many new people moving to the community, and they don’t really know much about the history of the buildings they drive past now,” said Rainey, a longtime documentarian, who has worked for National Geographic and the Discovery Channel. “We see people in Facebook groups, like Waterford Today or Simcoe, whatever, sort of saying, I think I know about this building, but they don’t know the truth.” “I thought you know what, Daryl’s in real estate and has an affinity for history and historic buildings, what if we told stories of these buildings so that people in these communities could know the history of what was there,” Rainey continued. Advertisement 3 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content The latest edition centres around Delhi and the Croton Dam, the town’s former velodromes, the Calvin Presbyterian Church, Quance Dam and Deltasia, a little-known 1970s fantasy amusement park. “I was doing some videos for VandenBussche Irrigation, and while interviewing the owner (Marc VandenBussche), we were talking about the history of the business, and he said in passing, his dad gave him and his sister 25 cents and they would go over to Deltasia, kill some time and play,” Rainey explained. A lightbulb went off, motivating Rainey to dig for more about the park built by W.C. “Bill” Kelsey. Following a trip to Disney World in the 1960s, Kelsey aimed to bring its magic back home with an amusement park on the outskirts of the town. Advertisement 4 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content Portions of the project today would never get off the ground due to copyright laws, but any potential issues never made it to the Disney company 50 years ago. “I was just captivated by it, so I was trying to hunt down anything I could, and nobody knew anything,” explained Rainey, a Delhi resident. “The (Delhi) museum didn’t have anything on it, but I luckily came across his grandson, Tim Warris, and it turns out they had a cornucopia of photos and 16 millimetre film and everything, so we were able to tell the story of this one-time amusement park, fantasy land here in Delhi, that existed during the ’70s. I’m really excited to show that.” “He built rides for the kids, a fountain and rocket ship, a robot out of an old washing machine tub complete with a hidden microphone and speaker,” Kelsey’s grandson Scott Warris wrote in an online blog. “He would spend hours hiding in the snack bar, carrying on conversations with bewildered kids mystified how the machine could hear them, and talk back too!” Advertisement 5 Story continues below This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below. Article content “At the time, there was no way I could appreciate just what those years would represent for the rest of my life,” Warris continued. “All the thousands of chores involved the learning of many skills, using tools and thinking things out.” The five short films will be shown on the big screen on November 30 at 2 and 4 p.m. at Capitol 33 in Delhi. Rainey said past episodes on Waterford (twice), Simcoe and Port Dover have been “a hit” with folks near and far. “We get tens of thousands of views on them; they’re very successful,” he said. “With this one, we took a different approach. We wanted to do something more in-person, more community-minded, and we wanted to do a premiere at the local theatre – Capital 33. It’s a beautiful spot. (Owner) Jordan (Gawley) and his team have supported some other projects we’ve done, so I’m really excited about this.” Both Rainey brothers will be joined by Andrew Moore, curator of the Delhi Tobacco Museum, to answer audience questions during the event. Tickets are $15 in advance (ticketscene.ca or capitol33.ca) and $20 at the door. Marking his third film following “A Star is Born” and “Maestro,” the film stars Will Arnett, Laura Dern, Andra Day, Bradley Cooper, Amy Sedaris, Sean Hayes, Christine Ebersole, Ciarán Hinds and Scott Icenogle. Arnett plays Alex, a man whose marriage quietly unravels. As he faces middle age and an impending divorce, he seeks new purpose in the New York comedy scene. Meanwhile, his wife Tess (Laura Dern) confronts the sacrifices she made for their family – forcing them to navigate co-parenting, identity, and whether love can take a new form. Cooper, Arnett and Mark Chappell penned the script for the film which served as the closing night selection of the New York Film Festival. “Is This Thing On?” will arrive exclusively in cinemas in December. This first premiered at the 2025 New York Film Festival as their big Closing Night gala ( view the teaser from then ), with a full theatrical release set for December coming up. If anyone wants to watch. As their marriage quietly unravels, Alex faces middle age and a divorce, seeking new purpose in the New York comedy scene; while his soon-the-be-ex-wife Tess confronts the sacrifices she made for the family—forcing them both to navigate co-parenting, identity, and whether love can take on a new form. Cooper\'s beautifully lived-in third feature is both lacerating and sweet-souled, funny, and tender. Inspired by the true story of British comedian John Bishop . The very dry comedy stars Will Arnett as Alex and Laura Dern as Tess, with Andra Day , Bradley Cooper , Amy Sedaris , Sean Hayes , Christine Ebersole , Ciarán Hinds , and Scott Icenogle . Reviews were mixed-to-good at the fests, saying the film is a "warm, essential reminder that it\'s never too late to grab the microphone and start telling our own story." It\'s worth a watch. Here\'s the official trailer (+ 3 new posters) for Bradley Cooper\'s film Is This Thing On? , from YouTube : You can rewatch the teaser trailer for Bradley Cooper\'s Is This Thing On? film right here for the first look. Intro via NYFF : In a pair of galvanizing, deeply honest performances, Will Arnett & Laura Dern play Alex & Tess Novak, whose marriage has reached an impasse. With amicable sorrow, the couple—parents of two young boys—mutually agree to split up. Yet in Cooper\'s keenly observed comic drama, their separation leads to unpredictable midlife self-reckonings, most dramatically in Alex\'s wild career pivot to become a confessional stand-up comedian in NYC\'s West Village, where he finds new direction & camaraderie. This seemingly outlandish scenario—in a script by Cooper, Arnett, and Mark Chappell inspired by the true story of British comedian John Bishop —is never played for easy laughs, while Cooper uses his penchant for naturalism to give the actors space to find their complicated centers. Is This Thing On? is directed by American actor / producer / filmmaker Bradley Cooper , director of the films A Star Is Born and Maestro previously; he also produced War Dogs , A Star Is Born , Joker , Nightmare Alley . The screenplay is written by Bradley Cooper, Will Arnett, and Mark Chappell. Produced by Weston Middleton, Kris Thykier, Cooper, Arnett. This is premiering at the 2025 New York Film Festival this fall. Searchlight Pictures opens Cooper\'s Is This Thing On? film in select US theaters starting on December 19th, 2025 coming soon. (Credit: Getty Images) “One Piece” has cast one of its antagonists for Season 3. Bon Clay will be played by Cole Escola , TheWrap has learned. Escola is perhaps best known for creating and starring in the Broadway show “Oh, Mary!” which won two Tony Awards earlier this year. They’ve also appeared in “Search Party” as well as “At Home with Amy Sedaris,” “Difficult People” and “Big Mouth.” In addition to winning a Tony for Best Performance by a Leading Actor in a Play, Escola was also a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize for Drama earlier this year. It’s pretty great casting. In the anime and manga, Bon Clay, also known as Bentham of the Wild, is defined by their love of wild looks and an eccentric, borderline manic fighting style. And no one in Hollywood captures oddly charismatic mania better than Escola. “A master of performance and precision, Bon Clay is as dangerous as they are dazzling — a theatrical assassin who turns combat into art,” a press release from Netflix reads. In the original story of “One Piece,” Bon Clay was a member of Miss Goldenweek’s Baroque Works as well as a major antagonist of the Straw Hats during the Arabasta Arc. But, as is often the case when it comes to Luffy, they eventually come to be one of his closest allies. Production for “One Piece” Season 3 will happen later this year in Cape Town, South Africa. More cast will be announced at a later date. Season 2, which is also known as “One Piece: Into the Grand Line,” will premiere on Netflix on March 10. The life of British comedian John Bishop inspired the movie’s story. The Hollywood Reporter film critic David Rooney writes of the comic drama in his New York Film Festival review: “In Cooper’s tenderly observed third feature, Is This Thing On? , performance is a rebound reflex, a therapeutic means of working through the end of a marriage and stumbling onto the self-discovery necessary to process what went wrong — inadvertently realizing that the foundations on which it was built remain intact. It’s an unassuming comic drama that sneaks up on you, its emotional honesty fueled by gorgeous performances of unimpeachable naturalness from Will Arnett and Laura Dern.” Is This Thing On? is Cooper’s directorial follow up to Maestro and his directorial debut with A Star Is Born . As with A Star Is Born and Maestro , Cooper is also part of the cast of his third film, the ensemble cast of which includes Andra Day, Christine Ebersole, Ciarán Hinds, Sean Hayes and Amy Sedaris. In fact, she shared her negative experience with taking Ozempic—a type 2 diabetes drug that can help people slim down due to its appetite-reducing properties—earlier this year. “I was like bedridden,” she explained during her appearance on The Howard Stern Show in January. “I was vomiting, and then you have no energy. The Muppets While there’s no official word from either Disney or The Jim Henson Company about the film’s development, and Lawrence didn’t share any plot details, this announcement guarantees fans will do everything they can to make sure it happens. It has to. Despite being one of the most vocal divas in history, Miss Piggy has never starred in her own film. And Escola—who wrote and won a Tony for starring in their Broadway smash comedy Oh, Mary! —is an absolutely perfect choice to capture Miss Piggy’s voice. Their other notable credits include At Home With Amy Sedaris , Tuca & Bertie , and Difficult People . If anyone can make The Muppets ‘ diva shine, Escola can. Published Sat, 08 Nov 2025 07:17:03 -0600 by Aedan Juvet | Comments Article Summary Jennifer\'s Body director Karyn Kusama confirms Diablo Cody is working on a sequel script right now The 2009 cult horror film gained a passionate following after an underwhelming box office debut Kusama promises the sequel will be as fun and wild as the original, staying true to its unique tone Fans and creators believe Jennifer\'s Body is finally getting the recognition it deserves in horror Sixteen years after release, Jennifer\'s Body keeps gaining ground. The 2009 teen horror from writer Diablo Cody and director Karyn Kusama follows Jennifer Check, a popular small-town cheerleader who becomes demonically possessed after a botched rock-band ritual, then begins feeding on male classmates. Her best friend Anita "Needy" Lesnicki pieces together the truth and fights to stop the killings, becoming a showdown that reframes high-school power dynamics through a sharp, darkly comic lens. The cast did a lot of the heavy lifting. Megan Fox leads as Jennifer, and Amanda Seyfried co-stars as Needy, with Adam Brody as frontman Nikolai, Johnny Simmons as Chip, J. K. Simmons as Mr. Wroblewski, and Amy Sedaris in support. The film premiered in 2009 after Cody\'s teen breakout hit Juno and quickly became a conversation piece about gender roles and media consumption, even as some viewers and critics missed what it was doing at the time. On paper, the numbers looked pretty underwhelming. Jennifer\'s Body cost about $16 million and grossed roughly $32 million worldwide in theaters, becoming a modest return that fueled the "flop" label before home release success and the cult following really kicked in. Yet the reassessment has been steady and loud. Many fans have argued the movie was mismarketed ahead of its release, and that its blend of friendship drama, anger, and satire reads much clearer now. Megan Fox as Jennifer in Jennifer\'s Body (2009). Image courtesy of 20th Century Studios Jennifer\'s Body Director on the Potential Sequel All of this essentially makes the recent sequel chatter feel even more earned. Both Cody and Fox have previously spoken positively about returning over the years, but now, Kusama has offered the most concrete signal yet. Speaking to Deadline , she said Cody is actively at work. "I know she\'s working on it right now, and I\'m very excited to hear what comes of it. I know some of the bones of it, so I\'m not going to give anything away, but it sounds fun and crazy like the first film. And I have no doubt that Diablo will do something absolutely incredible with it." At this point, it\'s obvious that Jennifer\'s Body has outlasted its first-weekend narrative. It found its audience, influenced a wave of feminist-leaning horror, and became a touchstone for teen terror (with teeth). Brining, baking and brand buzz By Deniz Ataman 25-Nov-2025 Last updated on 25-Nov-2025 at 14:55 GMT Thanksgiving 2025 trends show consumers embracing scratch-made comfort foods, premium upgrades and nostalgic brands, while retailers and brands compete on value. (Image: Tyler Darden) From budget-friendly feasts to playful twists, brands are blending affordability, nostalgia and creativity to win over holiday hosts This Thanksgiving, consumers are leaning into scratch-made comfort foods, premium upgrades and playful twists – while brands respond with value-driven deals and nostalgic favorites. Consumers are planning to cook and eat at home more this year compared to last year, according to recent data from Kroger’s 84.51 Precision Marketing’s consumer digest. On Thanksgiving, 82% of shoppers plan to share a sit-down meal with others and 66% plan to cook and bake at home. Consumers’ menu will revolve around scratch-made dishes like main courses, savory sides and fresh sides, while snacks and appetizers, desserts and breakfast will be made with mixes. Pre-made items like dinner breads and candy are expected to be present as well, according to 84.51. With Thanksgiving recipe searches up 32.9% year over year across Google, TikTok and Instagram, consumers are looking for staples and elevated ingredients to incorporate into their at-home menus, according to Spate search data from Oct. 2024 to Sept. 2025 vs. Oct. 2023 to Sept. 2024. Comfort, quality and nostalgia are driving holiday search behavior Searches for holiday staples are surging, like green beans, brine, turkey brine, egg and Gournay cheese all jumped more than tenfold year over year, signaling prep for casseroles, turkey brining, baking and cheese boards. Searches for cheese climbed +235% YoY to 63.0K searches, chicken rose +178.9% to 29.7K (a 19.0K increase YoY), and pantry staples like potato (110.2K, +24.2K) and sweet potato (83.1K, +28.5K) continue to anchor meal planning, per Spate. Searches for nostalgic and premium brands are also spiking. Velveeta tops the list with >1,000% YoY growth and 422.4K searches (+420.9K), followed by Boursin (255.8K; +249.8K) and Kerrygold (158.0K; +158.0K). Pantry staples like Campbell’s (+634%; 223.6K) and Kraft (+418%; 183.3K) are trending, while sweet treats and baking essentials – Lotus Biscoff and King Arthur Baking – also jumped more than tenfold, per Spate. International twists on traditional Thanksgiving dishes, like pumpkin tamales, butternut squash risotto, green-chile and jalapeno cornbread, key lime cranberry relish and oyster stuffing also are on the rise, according to Tastewise data . Sign in to your MovieWeb account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There is a reason so many horror movies are also coming-of-age stories. Puberty is a nightmare and while growing up is hard for everyone, there is something particularly monstrous in the shift from girlhood into womanhood . There is a lot that goes on biologically and socially during this time. The pressures placed on young girls by themselves, their peers, their parents, the media, and grown men who have no business weighing in at all certainly doesn\'t help. It\'s no wonder, then, that there are some pretty incredible horror movies highlighting the torments of girlhood. From the innocence of childhood to the chaos of one\'s teenage years, these movies explore the female experience with harrowing precision. They examine not only the horrors of girlhood, but also how different stressors, expectations, and influences contribute to those horrors. 10 \'Carrie\' (1976) United Artists Carrie is the first screen adaptation of Stephen King\'s classic 1974 debut novel. Sissy Spacek ( Coal Miner\'s Daughter ) stars as the quiet and sensitive Carrie White, a teenage girl who is ruthlessly bullied at her high school. The film was directed by Brian De Palma ( Scarface ) with a screenplay by Lawrence D. Cohen ( Ghost Story ). The cast features Amy Irving ( Crossing Delancey ), Nancy Allen ( The Philadelphia Experiment ), P. J. Soles ( Halloween ), William Katt ( Jawbreaker ), John Travolta ( Pulp Fiction ), Betty Buckley ( Tender Mercies ), and Piper Laurie ( The Hustler ) as Carrie\'s strict and fanatically religious mother, Margaret White. Public Humiliation Is De Palma the right director for this movie? Debatable. Is Sissy Spacek a phenomenal Carrie? Absolutely. Right from the beginning, the film jumps into the deep end of girlhood torment. Carrie gets her first period in the gym locker room at school. Since her mother has never explained menstruation to her, she thinks she is dying and panics. From there, Carrie develops telekinetic powers as the bullying intensifies and her mother\'s religious zeal reaches new heights. Carrie received two Academy Award nominations, Best Actress in a Lead Role for Sissy Spacek and Best Actress in a Supporting Role for Piper Laurie. Today, the movie is certified fresh with a 94% rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. 9 \'Poison for the Fairies\' (1986) Flavia becomes Veronica\'s prey in Poison for Fairies Colección IMCINE Poison for the Fairies , also known as Veneno para las hadas , is a Mexican supernatural horror film written and directed by Carlos Enrique Taboada ( The Book of Stone ). The film earned 10 nominations at the Ariel Awards, winning in five categories, including Best Picture and Best Direction. Ana Patricia Rojo ( Fugitivas, en busca de la libertad ) won Best Child Performance at the Bogota Film Festival and the SIlver Goddess Award for Best Child Acting from the Mexican Cinema Journalist. The film has an 80% rating from audiences on Rotten Tomatoes. Bullying and Black Magic Veronica (Rojo) is a young girl who fantasizes about being a witch to cope with her loneliness at school. When her class gets a new student, Flavia (Elsa María Gutiérrez), Vernonica covets Flavia\'s wealth and stable home life. So what does Veronica do? She convinces Flavia that she is a witch and forces her to partake in increasingly dangerous games. Veronica delights in the new power she holds over Flavia through this facade, a complete flip from the lack of control she felt when the other students were making fun of her. 8 \'The Craft\' (1996) Assumpta Serna in The Craft Sony Pictures Releasing The Craft is directed by Andrew Fleming ( Bad Dreams ), who also wrote the screenplay with Peter Filardi ( Chapelwaite ). Robin Tunney ( The Mentalist ) stars as Sarah Bailey, a teenage girl with unique abilities who moves to a new home with her family in Los Angeles, California. At her new school, she befriends Nancy Downs, Bonnie Harper, and Rochelle Zimmerman — played by Fairuza Balk ( Almost Famous ), Neve Campbell ( Scream ), and Rachel True ( Nowhere ). Together, the four outcasts form a coven. They become powerful witches , but as they seek revenge on those who have wronged them at school, the consequences become more extreme than they could have anticipated. We\'re the Weirdos, Mister While the mainstream media didn\'t give The Craft much credit upon release, the film received five Fangoria Chainsaw Award nominations and two Saturn Award nominations. This movie is an absolute cult classic today, despite mediocre reviews back in the 1990s. The line "We Are the Weirdos, Mister" has become iconic, adapted by contemporary women in horror almost as both affirmation and battle cry. The way the film tackles bullying, racism, and sexual double standards continues to resonate with audiences. 7 \'Ginger Snaps\' (2000) Motion International Ginger Snaps is a Canadian cult classic werewolf movie directed by Orphan Black co-creator John Fawcett with a screenplay by Orphan Black writer Karen Walton. Emily Perkins ( Stephen King\'s It ) and Katharine Isabelle ( American Mary ) star as Brigitte and Ginger Fitzgerald, two teenage sisters who are obsessed with death and are determined to get out of their suburban town, whatever the cost. One night, Ginger is bitten by a creature that\'s been attacking local dogs. In the days that follow, Brigitte starts to notice that her sister is changing in ways she can\'t explain — ways that might just be dangerous. Shades of David Cronenberg When we talk about girlhood and horror, Ginger Snaps is always going to come up. The movie is on just about every college syllabus for women in horror classes and this list wouldn\'t be complete without it. The film did well upon release, with critics comparing it to the work of David Cronenberg and Buffy the Vampire Slayer . Ginger Snaps earned seven Fangoria Chainsaw Award nominations, winning for Best Screenplay and Best Limited-Rlease/Direct-to-Video film. It won Best Canadian Feature Film Special Jury Citation at the Toronto International Film Festival and Best Movie at the International Horror Guild Awards. The movie is certified fresh with a 90% rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. 6 \'Teeth\' (2007) Roadside Attractions Written and directed by Mitchell Lichtenstein ( Angelica ), Teeth blends dark comedy and body horror for an unforgettable premise. The film stars Jess Weixler ( Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story ) as Dawn O\'Keefe, a high school student in a Christian abstinence group who discovers a startling fact about her own body during a sexual assault. She has vagina dentata, with teeth in her vagina that bite off her attacker\'s genitals. An Unexpected Adaptation Critics praised Teeth for the way it uses the relationship between horror and virginity in unexpected ways. Lichtenstein won the Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Festival and Jess Weixler was awarded a Special Jury Prize for her performance. The film scored three Fangoria Chainsaw Awards and was nominated for Best Feature Film at the Berlin International Film Festival. It\'s certified fresh on Rotten Tomatoes with an 81% score from critics. In 2024, Anna K. Jacobs and Michael R. Jackson adapted the film into an off-Broaday musical in New York. 5 \'Jennifer\'s Body\' (2009) Directed by legendary filmmaker Karyn Kusama (The Invitation) with a screenplay by Diablo Cody ( Lisa Frankenstein ), Jennifer\'s Body follows in the footsteps of Ginger Snaps , exploring the relationship between puberty and womanhood with the monstrous. Amanda Seyfried ( Things Heard & Seen ) stars as Anita "Needy" Lesnicki, a bookish high school student who is best friends with the popular Jennifer Check, played by Megan Fox ( Night Teeth ). The cast includes appearances by Adam Brody ( Ready or Not ), Kyle Gallner ( Strange Darling ), Johnny Simmons ( Scott Pilgrim vs. the World ), Amy Sedaris ( At Home with Amy Sedaris ), and J. K. Simmons ( Spider-Man ). How the Movie was Misunderstood Jennifer\'s Body is another movie that got rough reviews when it came out, but has since been reclassified as a cult classic. To give a sense of the mixed signals surrounding the film\'s release, Fox was nominated for Worst Actress at the Razzies but won Choice Movie Actress at the Teen Choice Awards. It\'s a prime example of what happens when marketing and expectations have a negative impact regardless of a film\'s intentions or actual merits. Jennifer\'s Body went from hated to loved in just a decade\'s time. It\'s a complex tale that explores themes of revenge, sexuality, and personhood. 4 \'The Witch\' (2015) A24 Robert Eggers made his feature film debut writing and directing The Witch . The folk horror drama stars Anya Taylor-Joy ( Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga ) as Thomasin, a teenage girl in a 1630s Puritan New England family who encounters witchcraft and possession after the disappearance of her younger brother. The cast includes Ralph Ineson ( Nosferatu ), Kate Dickie ( Dept. Q ), Harvey Scrimshaw ( The School for Good and Evil ), and Julian Richings ( Supernatural ). A Chilling Slow-Burn The Witch has been celebrated as an incredibly unnerving slow-burn that launched Taylor-Joy\'s career. The film won Best First Feature and Best First Screenplay at the Independent Spirit Awards. Taylor-Joy won Breakthrough Actor at the Gotham Awards and was nominated for Best Performance by a Younger Ator at the Saturn Awards. The Witch received five Fangoria Chainsaw Award nominations, winning Best FIlm and Best Actress for Anya Taylor-Joy. It is certified fresh with a 91% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. 3 \'Raw\' (2016) Wild Bunch Titane director Julia Ducournau made her feature film debut writing and directing Raw . This French coming-of-age body horror movie stars Garance Marillier ( Marinette ) as a vegetarian veterinary student who develops an unmanageable taste for human flesh. The cast includes Ella Rumpf ( Tiger Girl ), Rabah Naït Oufella ( The Class ), Joana Preiss ( Paris, Je T\'aime ), and Laurent Lucas ( Lemming ). \'Suspiria\' Meets \'Ginger Snaps\' Sisterhood, academia, and growing up are all explored in Raw as cannibalism is used as a metaphor. Variety called the movie " Suspiria meets Ginger Snaps ." Raw won the Directors\' Fortnight or Critics\' Week Prize at the Cannes Film Festival as well as the Citizen Kane Award for Best Directorial Revelation at the Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. It was nominated for six César Awards and won the Sutherland Award for First Feature at the London Film Festival. It is certified fresh on Rotten Tomatoes with a 93% rating from critics. 2 \'Piggy\' (2022) Filmax Carlota Pereda ( The Chapel ) wrote and directed Piggy , basing it on a short film she made in 2019 of the same name. Laura Galán ( Unknown Origins ), who also starred in the short film, plays Sara, a teen who is bullied for her weight by girls at the pool while she is on vacation. The bullies steal her backpack and clothes, forcing her to walk home in her bathing suit. When Sara realizes that her bullies have been kidnapped by an unknown stranger, she says nothing. Sharp Social Commentary Piggy is atmospheric and bloody with a sharp social commentary that explores the dangers of bullying . The film received four nominations at Spain\'s Cinema Writers Circle Awards with a win for Galán in the Best New Actress category. The movie received six nominations at the Goya Awards, again with a win for Galán in Best New Actress. She also won the Newcomer Award at the Spanish Actors Union. Piggy is certified fresh with a 91% rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. 1 \'Hatching\' (2022) Nordisk Film Hatching , also called Pahanhautoja , is a Finnish body horror movie directed by Hanna Bergholm ( Helsinki Crimes ) in her feature film debut and written by Ilja Rautsi ( Fleak ). Siiri Solalinna stars as 12-year-old Tinja, a young gymnast struggling with her mother\'s (Sophia Heikkilä) insistence that they present themselves as the perfect family. When Tinja finds what she thinks is a crow\'s egg, she brings it home and protects it from the elements. She hides the egg from her family, but when the egg catches, a strange human-sized bird-like creature emerges. Tinja names the creature Alli, but as Alli grows, Tinja the whole experience turns into a nightmare. Creepy Creature Effects The animatronics in Hatching are definitely disturbing. It\'s no wonder the film won Best Special Effects at the Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. Bergholm won the Grand Prize for Best Film and the Youth Jury Grand Prize at the Gérardmer Film Festival. Hatcing was also nominated for Best International Movie and Best Creature FX at the Fangoria Chainsaw Awards. The movie is certified fresh with a 93% rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. Today, we cover Larry David’s recent chat with Seth Meyers, The Daily Show’s Michael Kosta on the NBA betting scandal, John Oliver on Medicare, and a funny moment on The Tonight Show with Allen Iverson. “How can they live? I feel so sorry for them.” Such were the words of Larry David last week, describing on Late Night with Seth Meyers what he thinks every time he sees one of his children. The thought of his two daughters walking around with his genes was too much for the man to bear. Ever the perceptive interviewer, Seth Meyers then pivoted to asking Larry (referring to him as “David” somehow feels disrespectful, no?) about his own parents. “My mother had nothing to brag about,” Larry said, referring to himself. “The poor woman.” He went on to share that he never lived up to her high hopes—in other interviews, Larry has discussed how his parents hoped he would join up with one of our nation’s most honorable professions: the US Postal Service. Instead, as he explained here to Meyers, she was stuck with a then-failing comic. But Larry had a backup plan. His mother, he told Meyers, was like much of America, a massive fan of Johnny Carson. “She couldn’t stop talking about Johnny,” Larry said. “Oh, Johnny. You should have heard Johnny last night. Oh, Johnny was so funny.” That’s when he came up with a deathbed plan. “I wanted her to die happy,” he said. “So I came up with this plan that I would go into the hospital and I would say, ‘Ma, Ma, Johnny saw me perform last night. Johnny wants me on his show, Ma. Johnny likes me.’” Meyers, however, saw a flaw in this never-realized plan: “Do you think there was a chance that you’d tell her that and instead of her having one last happy moment, she would’ve died sad, being disappointed in Johnny Carson’s taste?” Always the honest man, Larry considered the thought before responding, “Quite possibly.” Sometimes, the rotating cast of hosts over on The Daily Show just works out too perfectly. Such are the beautiful ebbs and flows of the news cycle. And last week was one of those times , as former pro-athlete Michael Kosta was behind the desk to discuss the news that shocked the sports world: a betting scandal involving NBA players and the mob. Kosta had the take that went through the heads of NBA and Sopranos fans everywhere. “The mafia must really be hurting if the biggest NBA name they can get is Chauncey Billups,” Kosta said. “They couldn’t get Shaq? He’ll take money for anything.” Somewhere, Charles Barkley smiled. The other major star allegedly part of the deal is Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier. With the perspective of a former struggling athlete, Kosta had a unique take on Rozier’s involvement. “Jesus Christ, Terry. You’ve made over $160 million in your career. You shouldn’t be doing gambling schemes,” Kosta said. “Leave the schemes for the guys on the bench. They’re the ones who need the money.” But as always, Kosta turned back to being the moral compass of a confused and disappointed nation. “The NBA understands this scandal has really tarnished their integrity,” Kosta said. “That’s why the league is making it up to fans by offering them a $50 freeplay on FanDuel using the promo code JailBlazer.” “I’m gonna make it baby, come on, come on!” Over on Last Week Tonight, John Oliver addressed a topic of some importance: Medicare. Or, rather, something called Medicare Advantage, a supplement to the government program administered by private insurers. “They’re just not the same,” Oliver said. “It’s like the difference between a flashlight and a fleshlight.” Oliver begins by pointing out the slew of misleading advertisements targeting seniors during Medicare’s open enrollment period, which use the catch-all “Medicare” when they are actually referring to Medicare Advantage. He hilariously dissects these ads, which often feature celebrities, but are also sometimes long-form advertisements that play with “amateur porn level acting,” to borrow his phrase, with one spouse pleading with another to sign up for Medicare Advantage. You know, the kind of ad you would see on TV at 3 a.m. when you were up sick all night in the pre-streaming days. Oliver wonderfully plays one of these ad for far too long, only to reveal that it was only halfway over. “I also love the disclaimer saying ‘paid actor portrayal,\'” Oliver said, enlarging the screen. “As if we’d be so sucked in by the natural delivery of concussed Rob Reiner and over-caffeinated Amy Sedaris here that we’d need to be reminded.” But, as always, Oliver goes on to discuss the serious ramifications of these ads and the truth behind Medicare Advantage, which actually inflates, you’ll be shocked to learn, the cost of Medicare by bringing in private insurers. The upshot: among other flaws, insurers(yes, insurers) are able to add diagnoses to patients’ charts through a process called “upcoding,” essentially billing the government for treatments not actually given, for diagnoses unknown to patients and doctors. “The whole point of a doctor is for them to diagnose you,” Oliver said. “Or, in my case, for them to look at me, down at the chart, look at me again, back at the chart, and then say, ‘48 years old? Are we sure about that?’” And finally, a clip from The Tonight Show. Allen Iverson has been on the press circuit lately, promoting the docuseries about his life, Allen Iv3rson. Well, he and Jimmy Fallon couldn’t resist taking a trip down memory lane, reliving Iverson’s most memorable moment with the sports media, and indeed, perhaps the most famous press conference in sports history. Searle has been obsessed with storytelling since he was old enough to speak. He gravitated towards fairy tales, mythology, the fantasy genre, and animated movies and shows aimed at family audiences. When not writing, Tyler enjoys watching more cartoons and reading fantasy books in his home in Ontario, Canada. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Getting into a new television show can be a daunting thing. Whereas a movie only takes up a few hours to tell its story, television shows require a significantly larger investment to get to know the characters and see how the story unfolds. Thus, when a show isn't very good or gets worse later into its run, the disappointment stings even more. Fortunately, there are several animated shows out there that not only started strong but also improved with time . With the rise of streaming services and almost everything now available to watch online, they can be a constant source of entertainment for both returning fans and new ones discovering them for the first time. 10 'The Legend of Vox Machina' (2022–) Image via Prime Video When a mysterious monster begins to attack villages in the Tal'Dorei Empire, a call is put out for heroes to slay it. After all the best ones are brutally murdered, the only ones left are Vox Machina, a group of seven adventurers who can best be described as dysfunctional screw-ups. Still, they're the only heroes available, so Vox Machina will have to deal with their flaws and hang-ups if they're going to save the realm from the likes of dragons, necromancers, and other such threats to the realm. The Legend of Vox Machina is based on Critical Role's popular Dungeons & Dragons campaign, and does a great job translating the silly antics at the table to an epic high-fantasy series full of love, heartbreak, violence, and raunchy humor. The fact that the voice actors are friends and have been playing these characters for nearly a decade means that the interactions sound perfect, and sells Vox Machina as a found family trying to sort out their issues. The first season is a great setup, but come Season 2, the crew one-ups it with more impressive animation , grander set pieces, and even deeper character work that is continued into Season 3. 9 'Transformers: Prime' (2010–2013) Optimus Prime and Megatron clash blades in 'Transformers: Prime' Image via Hasbro Two factions of sentient robots from the planet Cybertron have taken their civil war to Earth. The noble Autobots, led by Optimus Prime ( Peter Cullen ), are on the back foot in their fight against the evil Decepticons, led by Megatron ( Frank Welker ), but find new allies among humans. They'll need all the help they can get because the Decepticons have dangerous ambitions related to raising the dead, and new threats emerge in the form of a human terrorist group called M.E.C.H., and a sadistic rogue Decepticon named Airachnid ( Gina Torres ). Transformers: Prime combined aspects from classic Transformers lore and the Michael Bay film series to create a show that had the best of both worlds. It featured strong-quality writing that wasn't afraid to go to dark places that showcased the horrors of war as best a family show could, while its small cast allowed each character to receive their own character arc. Even new characters introduced in later seasons were given enough attention to leave strong impressions, and the story got even more interesting as it introduced new factions and powerful Cybertronian artifacts. 8 'Teen Titans' (2003–2006) The Titans standing and looking skeptical. Image via Warner Bros. Animation On an island just off the coast of Jump City lies Titans Tower, home of the superheroes Robin ( Scott Menville ), Cyborg ( Khary Payton ), Raven ( Tara Strong ), Beast Boy ( Greg Cipes ), and Starfire ( Hynden Walch ). Together, they form the Teen Titans and fight to protect the city from all manner of threats, such as the masked mastermind Slade ( Ron Perlman ). When they're not saving the city, the Titans navigate the difficulties of five teens trying to live together, or sometimes going on wacky adventures. Teen Titans was one of the dominant superhero shows of the 2000s, and the voice actors were so perfectly chosen that they returned for the more lighthearted Teen Titans Go! Their camaraderie is the show's greatest strength, and only gets better with each season as they settle more into their roles, develop a better repertoire, and each season focuses on the development of a different Titan. Despite how weird some of its episodes could be, Teen Titans also knew when to get serious, with episodes focusing on heavy themes like obsession, self-destruction, prejudice, and showing vulnerability to those you love. 7 'Star Wars: The Clone Wars' (2008–2020) R2-D2, Anakin Skywalker, and Mace Windu in 'Star Wars: The Clone Wars' Image via Cartoon Network The galaxy finds itself divided by the Clone Wars, fought between the Galactic Republic, fielding an army of clone soldiers, and the Confederacy of Independent Star Systems, using legions of battle droids. Leading the armies of the Republic are the Jedi, warrior-monks who can manipulate an unseen energy called The Force and wield energy weapons called Lightsabers. The war is fought across many worlds, from the battlefields of once peaceful planets to the dark underbelly of major cities and the cutthroat landscape of politics. Star Wars: The Clone Wars was born from George Lucas' desire to explore more stories set during the divisive prequel trilogy, and became one of the most beloved Star Wars shows. During its nearly 140-episode run, the show covered all sorts of Star Wars storylines , with debates about the ethics of war, a look at how war affects the lives of the innocent as well as the soldiers, and crime lords trying to seize power in the chaos, just scratching the surface. Some of the best episodes focused on the clone soldiers ( Dee Bradley Baker ), who, as the seasons go on, transform from flesh robots like they were in the movies to fully fleshed-out characters with their own personalities and opinions on the conflict. 6 'Justice League (2001–2004) / 'Justice League Unlimited' (2004–2006) Justice League Unlimited animated series cast. Image via Warner Bros. Animation After working together to save the world from an alien invasion, Superman ( George Newbern ), Batman ( Kevin Conroy ), Wonder Woman ( Susan Eisenberg ), Green Lantern ( Phil LaMarr ), The Flash ( Michael Rosenbaum ), Martian Manhunter ( Carl Lumbly ), and Hawkgirl ( Maria Canals-Barrera ), decide to form a superhero team called the Justice League. From their Watchtower that orbits the Earth, they answer threats that are too big for any one hero to overcome. Later on, they expanded their roster to include even more heroes, though adversity would once again raise its head in the form of supervillain team-ups and government organizations. Justice League and Justice League Unlimited are really one show split over two different formats: the former told its stories through multi-episode storylines, while the latter was a more traditional half-hour episode. Season 1 can feel a bit slow as it's setting up the league members who hadn't appeared in previous DC shows, but it quickly finds its footing and jumps into bigger action with each subsequent season . The storylines were also very impressive for a kids' show, and often showcased that the reason these characters were superheroes wasn't their powers, but their hearts and how much they were willing to sacrifice for others. 5 'Gravity Falls' (2012–2016) The cast of Gravity Falls in a cave during the Weirdmageddon finale. Image via Disney XD Twin siblings Dipper ( Jason Ritter ) and Mabel Pines ( Kristen Schaal ) spend the summer at Gravity Falls with their great uncle, Stan ( Alex Hirsch ), who runs a tourist trap called the Mystery Shack with his slacker receptionist, Wendy ( Linda Cardellini ), and faithful handyman, Soos (Hirsch). On his first day, Dipper discovers a strange journal that details many strange, paranormal events in the town's history. The more Dipper explores them, the more he discovers that the mysteries are tied to his family and involve an otherworldly entity named Bill Cipher (Hirsch). Gravity Falls was the beginning of a new era of cartoons for Disney , and inspired future projects like Amphibia and The Owl House . The show's success came from its ability to juggle a compelling mystery that rewarded attention to detail, hilarious comedy, and solid character work. Gravity Falls Season 2 took all of this even further when it revealed exactly who wrote the journal and what happened to them, before ending on its own terms rather than continuing into seasonal rot. 4 'Adventure Time' (2010–2019) Adventure Time characters standing together on a cropped poster. Image via Cartoon Network The land of Ooo is a crazy fantasy land divided into themed kingdoms like candy, breakfast, and slime, which are beset by many dangers. Fortunately, it has protection in the form of two heroes: Finn the human ( Jeremy Shada ), an energetic adventurer, and Jake the dog ( John DiMaggio ), a shapeshifting dog and Finn's adopted brother. Their adventures bring them in contact with many fantastical characters, including the scientifically-minded Princess Bubblegum (Hynden Walch), the princess-stealing Ice King ( Tom Kenny ), and a carefree vampire named Marceline ( Olivia Olson ). Adventure Time began as a Dungeons & Dragons- style adventure show, with plenty of quests, random humor, and creative monsters. However, it quickly matured alongside its audience, with later seasons touching on abstract and metaphysical concepts like life, death, the purpose of existence, and more, without losing its original premise. This helped broaden the show's viewer base, and later spawned the spinoffs Adventure Time: Distant Lands and Adventure Time: Fionna and Cake , which continued the later seasons' trend of pushing the characters into more mature situations. 3 'Avatar: The Last Airbender' (2005–2008) Aang air-gliding with a large smile in Avatar: The Last Airbender. Image via Nickelodeon As the Fire Nation prepared for a war of conquest against the entire world, they eradicated the Air Nomads in an attempt to kill the Avatar, the only being who could master all four elements. 100 years later, the Avatar, a young boy named Aang ( Zach Tyler Eisen ), is found frozen in ice at the South Pole by Water Tribe siblings Katara ( Mae Whitman ) and Sokka ( Jack De Sena ). They decide to travel with Aang to help him master the other three elements, while avoiding pursuit by Zuko ( Dante Basco ), the disgraced prince of the Fire Nation, who seeks to capture Aang and return home with honor. Avatar: The Last Airbender has gone down as one of the greatest fantasy shows for kids and adults thanks to its brilliant writing, lovable characters, and immersive worldbuilding. The show was not afraid to tackle hard issues for kids, like the horrors of war, imperialism, free choice, and the morality of pacifism, and each of its characters has their worldview challenged during the journey that forces them to change, not always for the better. Season 1 was pretty good at setting up the world as the group traveled to the North Pole, but Season 2 introduced more characters who quickly became fan favorites, while Season 3 brought the characters into the heart of the Fire Nation itself. 2 'Batman: The Animated Series' (1992–1995) Batman's shadow standing atop a rooftop in front of buildings in Batman The Animated Series. Image via Warner Bros. Animation Gotham City is a haven of crime and corruption, making it difficult for its citizens to feel safe at night. Fortunately, when the sun goes down, Gotham is protected by its Dark Knight, Batman (Conroy). Aided by his ward, Robin ( Loren Lester ), his butler Alfred ( Clive Revill and Efrem Zimbalist Jr. ), and Police Commissioner Gordon ( Bob Hastings ), Batman regularly faces off against both small-time gangsters and powerful supercriminals, including the Joker ( Mark Hamill ), The Penguin ( Paul Williams ), Poison Ivy ( Diane Pershing ), and Ra's al Ghul ( David Warner ). Batman: The Animated Series broke new ground for superhero shows with its mature storytelling , and shaped an entire generation's perspective of these characters to the point that DC Comics made adjustments to certain characters to match the show's versions, and adopted the character of Harley Quinn ( Arleen Sorkin ). People fell in love with its dark atmosphere and willingness to explore why the villains act the way they do, making them sympathetic without justifying their actions. The show's later season saw a change to its art style to better fit with Superman: The Animated Series , which was a bit hit-and-miss, but many of the episodes remained just as powerful as ones from the early seasons. 1 'BoJack Horseman' (2014–2020) Princess Carolyn (Amy Sedaris) having dinner with BoJack Horseman (Will Arnett) in Season 1, Episode 1 of BoJack Horseman. Image via Netflix In the 1990s, BoJack Horseman ( Will Arnett ) starred in the hit sitcom Horsin' Around, but has since fallen into a rut full of alcohol, drugs, sex, and nihilism. He decides to publish his memoirs to get back into the public eye and teams up with ghostwriter Diane Nguyen ( Alison Brie ) to get it written. Along the way, BoJack has various humorous and reflective adventures with Diane, his roommate Todd ( Aaron Paul ), his longtime agent Princess Carolyn ( Amy Sedaris ), and his former sitcom rival Mr. Peanutbutter ( Paul F. Tompkins ). BoJack Horseman 's first season starts a little rocky, but by the time it ends, you can't wait to jump into Season 2 and see where things will develop. From there, the writing gets sharper and funnier, resulting in a show that encourages the audience to take a deep, hard look at themselves and their flaws through its characters. It's been almost 25 years since the hit film was released, so we're taking a look back at the 2000 movie cast then and now. By: Vivian Reading Time: 5 minutes November 10, 2025 9:45AM EST Breadcrumbs Navigation See Pics Entertainment Entertainment Features Jim Carrey Image Credit: Getty Images The love for The Grinch always spikes during the holiday season — and this year marks a major milestone. How the Grinch Stole Christmas hit theaters on November 17, 2000, making it 25 years since Jim Carrey first brought Dr. Seuss ’ classic story to life on the big screen. The green grump has only become more beloved with time, continuing to dominate holiday TV schedules, TikTok makeup tutorials, and endless meme culture. Dr. Seuss’ tale has been reimagined many times over the decades, but there’s still nothing quite like Carrey’s iconic take on the Christmas curmudgeon. In honor of the film’s 25th anniversary, we’re taking a look back at the Whos of Whoville and where the cast is now — including Taylor Momsen , who went from sweet little Cindy Lou Who to full-blown rockstar. See the cast then and now below. Jim Carrey Jim Carrey played the Grinch. (Everett Collection/MEGA) Jim Carrey starred as the one and only Grinch in the 2000 film. Jim completely transformed into the iconic holiday character, spending 2 hours in the makeup chair at the start of the day, and one hour after filming was over. The Grinch remains one of Jim’s most beloved roles. In the years after How the Grinch Stole Christmas , Jim starred in notable films like Bruce Almighty , Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind , Lemony Snicket’s A Series of Unfortunate Events , and more. He starred in the hit film Sonic the Hedgehog in 2020 and reprised the role of Dr. Robotnik in the sequel. Jim returned to television for the Showtime series Kidding , which ran for 2 seasons. Jim was nominated for Best Actor – Television Series Musical or Comedy in 2019. He portrayed Joe Biden during SNL season 26. Jim dated Jenny McCarthy from 2005 to 2010. He met Cathriona White in 2012. Cathriona died by suicide in 2015. Jim was a pallbearer at her funeral. He dated Ginger Gonzaga for less than a year. Taylor Momsen Taylor Momsen played Cindy Lou Who. (Melinda Sue Gordon/Imagine Ent/Kobal/Shutterstock/Gregory Pace) Taylor Momsen was just 7 years old when she starred as Cindy Lou Who in How the Grinch Stole Christmas . She went on to appear in other films in the years after playing Cindy Lou, but her big break wouldn’t come until 2007 when she was cast as Jenny Humphrey on Gossip Girl . Taylor ended up leaving the series after season 4 in 2011. That same year, Taylor announced she was quitting acting to focus on her music career. She did return for the Gossip Girl series finale in 2012. In 2023, Taylor reunited with her Gossip Girl co-star Penn Badgley for an episode of his Podcrushed podcast. Since then Taylor has fully transitioned into music as the frontwoman of The Pretty Reckless. In September 2025 the band released “For I Am Death” — their first new song in four years — signaling a new era. Christine Baranski Christine Baranski played Martha May Whovier. (Everett Collection/MEGA) Christine Baranski starred as Martha May Whovier in the classic holiday film. Following How the Grinch Stole Christmas , Christine appeared in films like Chicago , A Bad Moms Christmas , as well as Mamma Mia! and its sequel. Her most defining TV role has been Diane Lockhart on The Good Wife (2009–2016), for which she earned multiple Emmy nominations, followed by the spinoff The Good Fight (2017–2022). More recently, she’s starred as Agnes van Rhijn in The Gilded Age (2022 – present), whose third season wrapped in 2025 with record viewership. Behind the scenes, Christine continues to earn accolades: she will receive the Achievement in Television Excellence Award at the 2025 ATX TV Festival. On the personal front, Christine was married to actor and playwright Matthew Cowles until his death in 2014; they have two daughters together, Isabel and Lily . Jeffrey Tambor Jeffrey Tambor played Mayor Augustus MayWho. (Everett Collection/MEGA) Jeffrey Tambor played Mayor Augustus MayWho, the Grinch’s nemesis. His other notable roles include Tom Manning in the Hellboy movies and Sid Garner in The Hangover trilogy. Jeffrey starred in the Amazon Prime Video series Transparent as Maura Pfefferman, a divorced transgender woman. The actor won a Golden Globe and 2 Emmys for his performance. Following allegations of sexual misconduct, Jeffrey was fired from the show and did not return for its fifth season. The actor starred as George Bluth Sr. in the series Arrested Development . The show originally ran from 2003 to 2006. Netflix picked up the show for a fourth season in 2013. Jeffrey returned for the fifth season of Arrested Development in 2019 despite the allegations against him. Jeffrey married his wife Kasia Ostlun in 2001. They have 4 children together. Molly Shannon Molly Shannon played Betty Lou Who. (Everett Collection/MEGA) Molly Shannon played Betty Lou Who, Cindy Lou Who’s mom. Molly was already a famous comedian when she was cast in How the Grinch Stole Christmas . In the year after the holiday film was released, Molly left Saturday Night Live . Molly has starred in movies like Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby , Me and Earl and the Dying Girl , Private Life , and more. Molly has balanced both comedic and dramatic roles. She’s also voiced the role of Wanda in the Hotel Transylvania film series and starred in the HBO comedy series Divorce , which ran for 3 seasons. Recently, she starred in The White Lotus, The Other Two , and I Love That For You . The actress married Fritz Chestnut in 2004. They have two children together. Bill Irwin Bill Irwin played Lou Lou Who. (Everett Collection/MEGA) Bill Irwin starred as Lou Lou Who, Cindy’s father. Bill went on to recur on CSI: Crime Scene Investigation and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit . He’s best known as Mr. Noodle, who appears in the “Elmo’s World” segments on Sesame Street . His notable film roles include Interstellar , Across the Universe , and Rachel Getting Married . Bill also starred in the FX series Legion , which ran from 2017 to 2019. The actor also appeared in the TV series The Dropout and films like Spoiler Alert and Rustin.
