Col. Joanne Hirst discussed, on Nov. 10, her life as a member of the U.S. Army Reserves as the guest speaker at the annual Crystal River Woman’s Club’s Veteran’s Luncheon for Military Women. Margo Wilson / Chronicle correspondent If Joanne Hirst had her way, every teen upon graduating from high school would join the military. Not a community service program. Not college. Not the family business. The military. In an interview and at a luncheon honoring female veterans, Hirst spoke about her 36 years as a member of the U.S. Army Reserve. She retired in 2011 as a lieutenant colonel and a nurse practitioner. Her life wasn’t easy, and, in some ways, her military service made it more difficult. But in many ways, her service made her life more interesting, focused and easier. “There is not a child mature enough to go straight into college,” she said in the interview. As a member of the Female Veterans Network of Citrus County, Hirst visits schools as part of the Citrus County School District’s Veterans in the Classroom program. And she tells of encountering a student who said his occupational goal was “to flip burgers.” Others tell her they want to be tattoo artists or nail technicians. But these aren’t jobs that students can count on to carry them through their lifetimes, as Hirst sees it. “They need structure to grow up and they’re not getting it at home,” she said. “They need regular structure and guidance. They need someone to tell them to pick up their dirty underwear.” Moreover, the military has “a job for everyone,” according to Hirst. What’s more, the military will train you in many different areas and also will pay for you to attend college. That’s how Hirst got to be a nurse practitioner. From left, Cheryl Devoid, Air Force; Carrie Schmid, Air Force; Joanne Hirst, Army; Merrily LeVee, Navy; Carol L. Phillips, Air Force; and Cynthia Henderson, Air Force, attended on Nov. 10 the annual Crystal River Woman’s Club’s Veteran’s Luncheon for Military Women. Hirst was the guest speaker. Henderson founded the Female Veterans Network of Citrus County. Photos by Margo Wilson / Chronicle correspondent A single mom’s path At the Crystal River Woman’s Club’s annual Veteran’s Luncheon for Military Women, guest speaker Hirst told how she went from being a 24-year-old single mom clerk typist, working at a hospital, to enlisting as an Army reservist in 1975 when she heard about the benefits some reservist coworkers were receiving. “I was ready to go back to school,” she said. She joined the Reserves as a corporal and clerk-typist but after a couple of years, signed up for a medic’s course. Next, she had the opportunity to study to be a licensed practical nurse, so she did. Then came an associate degree in applied science, and then she studied to be a registered nurse. Her Bachelor of Science degree in nursing followed. She said her “thirst for knowledge” spurred her to pursue her education. Then, one day, she received information from her alma mater, SUNY Polytechnic Institute of Utica, New York, that the school was starting a master’s degree program for nurse practitioners. Hirst signed up for that, too. “Finally, I knew what I wanted to do when I grew up,” she said. She said she started her educational pursuits in 1978, when her son, Brian, was 8. When she graduated as a nurse practitioner in 1997, Brian brought his 2-day-old daughter, Sabine, to the commencement, straight from the hospital. Nursing and engineering graduates cradled Sabine and passed her around as part of the festivities. Military and civilian service All the time Hirst was in the Reserves, she held civilian jobs, too. She worked in various positions at the Schoharie County Health Department in New York. She was an RN on a hospital surgery floor. As a nurse practitioner, she worked at a doctor’s office that was affiliated with a hospital. There, she counseled young women who might be having their first OB-GYN exam or helped seniors who might need home health care or transportation. While she was attending SUNY Polytech, she’d leave work about 4:30 p.m. and then drive over an hour twice a week, “following the snowplow,” to get to her classes starting at 6 p.m. When she was home, she frequently had a book in her hand. She told of attending Brian’s ballgames, nose poked in a book, and relying on others to tell her, “Brian’s up to bat.” Even though her attention was split, “I was always present,” she said. “I’m a good mom.” She credits her late husband, Charles, whom she met at her military unit’s Christmas party in 1975 and married in 1978, for pitching in when she couldn’t. Charles also was a reservist and a licensed practical nurse, as well as a mechanic and electrical specialist. Serving abroad Although Hirst spent many of her years as a nurse in New York State, as a reservist, she served at Army humanitarian clinics in Guatemala and Honduras in the late 1990s, seeing up to 1,400 people a day. She also supervised clinics in Germany in 2004-05 and ended her military career at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, helping launch the Wounded Warrior project. Her time at humanitarian clinics in Guatemala and Honduras left an impression. She told of how villagers would walk for hours to attend the clinics. “We’re in Crystal River,” she said. “It would be like if they walked in from Inverness or Inglis.” One villager rode in on a Brahman cow and somehow, the cow stepped on the woman’s foot and broke it. A man put the woman on his horse and led the horse to the hospital, Hirst said. Other villagers would have bacterial infections, and the doctors and nurses would give medication to clear up the infections. But when the villagers returned to their villages and the two- to three-week clinic had moved on, the villagers most likely were reinfected by the water or whatever source initially had caused their infection. The medical personnel served one remote village that a few months later was destroyed in a hurricane, and many of the people whom the medical people had treated died in the storm. Still, being able to care for others was a privilege, according to Hirst, who describes herself as “a nurturer …. I wanted to be a nurse ever since second grade.” Nurses, she said, “see everything. We have the information. We watch everything …. And, we have a smile.” Facing challenges Hirst is one who keeps smiling, even though she’s faced her share of difficulties. She is a three-time cancer survivor. Her husband passed away in 2018. But Hirst keeps going. “I try to be a mentor to other women,” she said. As historian for the Female Veterans Network, she’s found a supportive group that “is my lifeline, we are family …. “I have an excellent system with Female Veterans Network, and that’s what you need. You need to develop that, one way or another. Even if you’re in a shelter, they will help you …. There is always hope.” The Female Veterans Network can be reached at 352-628-6481. The Crystal River Woman’s Club can be reached at 352-795-5488. At Monday’s luncheon, club President Becky Culver gave the invocation. Crystal River High School’s Navy Junior Reserve Officers Training Corps presented the colors. Army veteran Carole Jasler led the National Anthem and the singing of military songs. Woman’s Club member Margie Harper led the blessing, and the club’s first vice president and event organizer Leslie Martineau welcomed those attending. Libby Wentzell was in charge of door prizes. Ana Segovia, district aide with U.S. Rep. Gus Bilirakis, welcomed the group. Hirst received a quilt from the Rainbow Quilters of Citrus Springs. Phyllis Smith was a real-life “Rosie the Riveter” during World War II and made manifolds for B-29 bombers. She’s a 27-year member of the Woman’s Club of Crystal River and spoke briefly at the club’s luncheon on Nov. 10 honoring female military veterans. Margo Wilson / Chronicle correspondent Nonagenarian Phyllis Smith spoke briefly about serving as a real-life “Rosie the Riveter” during World War II, making manifolds for B-29 bombers at a factory in Elmira, New York. She was 16 when she started working at the factory, having to quit school to help support her family. She’s been a member of the Woman’s Club for 27 years. Martineau said women like Smith helped open the doors for women to work in many fields. “You were a revolutionary and you didn’t know it,” she said. The Women of the Moose of Dunnellon Lodge 2308 presented the Crystal River Woman’s Club with a check for $500 on Nov. 10 at a luncheon the Woman’s Club hosted for military female veterans. Becky Culver, at left, is president of the Woman’s Club and Alma Whitman, center, is senior regent with the Women of the Moose. Also at the luncheon, the Women of the Moose of Dunnellon Lodge 2308, presented the Woman’s Club with a check for $500 from the Moose’s Valued Veterans Committee. Alma Whitman, senior regent of the Women of the Moose, said the Moose wanted to acknowledge the contributions the Woman’s Club makes and to also help out a bit, since the club’s building was twice damaged by hurricanes recently. The club has sold its former clubhouse and rents space from First Baptist Church of Crystal River. A woman in her 20s and a man in his 60s were killed, while a second woman in her 20s was flown to hospital with hearing damage and shock. The Endeavor Mine was closed for maintenance in 2020 but began operating again in June. Ciaran Mullooly, an Irish member of the European Parliament, remembered working with Mr McMullen in the 1980s. "Ambie was a treasured colleague … (he) was a lovely man, great fun and craic and we enjoyed many\'s (sic) the night out," he posted on Facebook. "RIP Ambie, farewell old friend." "He left Cootehill in the mid-1980\'s to travel and found a new home and life down under in Australia," his former classmate and local councillor Carmel Brady said. Flowers have been left at the Cobar Miners Memorial. (Samantha Smith/AAP PHOTOS) The explosion has thrust the sector\'s safety systems into the spotlight. University of Queensland mining safety expert David Cliff said it was rare for such incidents to occur and he believed it was an avoidable tragedy. But the professor, who previously served as a health and safety adviser to the Queensland Mining Council, said it was not clear whether the incident was the result of human error, machine failure or premature detonation. He pointed to several factors, including possible gaps in institutional knowledge with mining operations restarting in 2025 after ASX-listed Polymetals acquired the site in 2023. (Samantha Smith/AAP PHOTOS) Along with its Cobar mine, Polymetals holds two licences in Guinea, where it has previously explored for gold. Mining and Energy Union NSW district president Bob Timbs said a "catastrophic failure of a safety system" would have caused the deaths. The NSW Resources Regulator confirmed it would steer an incident investigation, while police will also prepare a report for the coroner. The site, 40km north of Cobar, is a major underground silver, zinc and lead mine. It is the second-largest project in the resource-rich region. Login or signup to continue reading All articles from our website The digital version of Today\'s Paper All other regional websites in your area Continue A young woman and man were killed by the explosion in the Endeavour mine at Cobar on Tuesday, which experts say appeared to be an avoidable tragedy. Early investigations conducted by the NSW Resources Regulator have revealed workers were tasked with preparing a ballistic disc device to clear a blockage in the mine\'s opening. But it was unintentionally set off, charging the fatal explosion. In a release published on Friday, regulators call on mine operators to reconsider their use of the ballistic disc, and look for alternatives. They also urge mine operators to review their risk assessments regarding the use of explosives on site. One mining safety expert believes the fatal incident at the Cobar mine was an avoidable tragedy. (Dan Peled/AAP PHOTOS) Ballistic disc explosives are designed to allow workers to safely clear blockages, without having to enter unstable areas in order to manually place dynamite charges. Definitive factors contributing to the incident are yet to be identified, according to the regulators. They are engaging with all parties involved in the manufacture, supply or use of the ballistic disc devices, as well as SafeWork NSW. Supply and use of explosives may be prohibited if the regulator finds use of the charges involves a serious risk to the health or safety of people. The explosion has thrust the sector\'s safety systems into the spotlight. The lead and zinc mine had operated since 1982 but was put into "care and maintenance" mode in 2020. University of Queensland mining safety expert David Cliff said it was rare for such incidents to occur and he believed it was an avoidable tragedy. But the professor, who previously served as a health and safety adviser to the Queensland Mining Council, said it was not clear whether the incident was the result of human error, machine failure or premature detonation. He pointed to several factors, including possible gaps in institutional knowledge with mining operations restarting in 2025 after ASX-listed Polymetals acquired the site in 2023. Along with its Cobar mine, Polymetals holds two licences in Guinea where it has previously explored for gold. The site, 40km north of Cobar, is a major underground silver, zinc and lead mine and the second-largest project in the resource-rich region. All Rights Reserved 15 Years Ago, The Most Hated Saw Movie Still Made A Killing At The Box Office NEWS MOVIES TV TRAILERS REVIEWS EXCLUSIVES FEATURES Newsletter Movies Horror Movies 15 Years Ago, The Most Hated Saw Movie Still Made A Killing At The Box Office By Ryan Scott Nov. 1, 2025 11:30 am EST Lionsgate ( Welcome to Tales from the Box Office , our column that examines box office miracles, disasters, and everything in between, as well as what we can learn from them. ) "Starting with the release of \'Saw VI,\' and the disappointing box-office performance, it\'s been a dark time for me, no question." Those are the words of longtime "Saw" franchise editor and director Kevin Greutert, speaking with Entertainment Weekly in 2010 ahead of the release of "Saw 3D." At the time, the movie was also known as "Saw: The Final Chapter," seeking to put an end to the saga of Jigsaw after seven consecutive years of cinematic carnage. Director James Wan\'s "Saw" became an unexpected box office smash in 2004 , pulling in $103 million worldwide against a minuscule $1.2 million budget. Lionsgate then made it an annual tradition. But as Greutert points out, despite being well-liked by devotees of the franchise, "Saw VI" made just shy of $70 million, by far the lowest-grossing entry up to that point. All the same, Lionsgate wanted the director to finish what he started with one last hoorah. It would go down as the worst-rated movie in the history of the franchise. Despite itself, it was also a major financial success. In this week\'s Tales from the Box Office, we\'re looking back at "Saw 3D" in honor of its 15th anniversary. We\'ll go over how it came to be, why Greutert was essentially forced into directing it, what happened when it hit theaters, what happened in the aftermath of its release, and what lessons we can learn from it all these years later. Let\'s dig in, shall we? The movie: Saw 3D Lionsgate As a fierce battle rages over Jigsaw\'s (Tobin Bell) terrible legacy, survivors seek support from a fellow survivor and self-help guru named Bobby Dagen (Sean Patrick Flanery), who harbors a dark secret. Namely, he lied about surviving one of Jigsaw\'s games to achieve fame and fortune. Meanwhile, crooked cop Hoffman (Costas Mandylor) seeks revenge against Jigsaw\'s wife as well as Dagen for his lies. As a franchise, despite coming off a low point with "Saw VI," it\'s worth pointing out that this was still a wildly consistent moneymaker for Lionsgate. Even that movie was made on an $11 million budget, meaning it was more than profitable for the studio. A bit of the problem is that "Saw V" was viewed as such a downgrade for the series that it hurt "VI" financially, despite the fact that it was a major improvement, critically speaking. Lionsgate wanted to lean into the good they had going. They certainly weren\'t going to go back to "Saw V" director David Hackl. They had every intention of leaning once again on Greutert\'s talents, as he had been with the series as an editor dating back to the original. More on that in a moment. As for the pitch? Timing was everything here, and Hollywood\'s 2000s 3D craze was off to the races. That was in no small part thanks to James Cameron\'s 2009 sci-fi smash "Avatar," which made more than $2.7 billion in its original run , becoming the highest-grossing movie of all time up to that point. Lionsgate wanted Jigsaw to get in on the trend. The Saw franchise had been chasing its tail for years up to this point Lionsgate At that particular moment in time, the franchise needed a hook. Part of the problem is that the "Saw" franchise had been chasing its tail for several years, becoming an accidental victim of its own success. Early on in the series, it was revealed that Tobin Bell\'s John Kramer, aka Jigsaw, had incurable cancer that was going to kill him. It did indeed kill him relatively early on, with Kramer kicking the bucket at the end of "Saw III." From then on, it was about others carrying on Kramer\'s work in his stead, with Amanda (Shawnee Smith) and Detective Hoffman largely carrying that torch. By the end of "Saw IV," Kramer\'s legacy was firmly in Hoffman\'s hands . Even so, the series needed Bell on board, finding ways to force him in through flashbacks, old recordings, etc. It would be like trying to continue the "Nightmare on Elm Street" franchise without Freddy. It was difficult. Series producers Mark Burg and Oren Koules later admitted that killing John Kramer so early on was a mistake . All the same, what\'s done was done, and to get around that glaring issue, the "Saw" franchise timeline got increasingly wonky and the twists got wackier. The series never fully managed to escape the shadow that Bell\'s Jigsaw cast over it. That was something that the so-called "Final Chapter" needed to contend with. Saw 3D wasn\'t made under the best of circumstances Lionsgate Around this time, another major horror franchise launched into the spotlight in the form of "Paranormal Activity," one of the most surprising hits in box office history . On a shoestring budget, it made $194 million worldwide, with Paramount moving quickly on a sequel. They originally tapped Greutert to helm what would become "Paranormal Activity 2." He even spent months developing the project. Then, Lionsgate stepped in. Deciding to exercise an option on his contract, Lionsgate forced Greutert to direct "Saw 3D," pulling him away from "Paranormal Activity 2." On his personal blog in January 2010 , in a post that was later deleted, Greutert expressed strong dissatisfaction with the situation, saying the following: "Woo hoo! Lawyers are sending me to Canada tomorrow! I just had the task of telling my 83 year old mother that no, I\'m not going to be allowed to direct the movie we were all so excited about when my family last got together, and that I\'m being forced to leave town before getting a chance to see her again. Yes, I\'ll be filming people getting tortured YET AGAIN. So we\'ll have to put off me making a film she can actually watch for another year. I\'m not making this s*** up." "There was a lot of crazy turmoil in this production," Greutert later said in that same, pre-release EW interview. "Frankly, I\'m glad it\'s over. Because there were definitely things that I would have done a lot differently if I had been on the film from the beginning. But at the same time, they wouldn\'t have brought me on so suddenly and at the last minute if they didn\'t trust my opinion." The financial journey Greutert largely played ball during the press tour, but there\'s no denying he wouldn\'t have chosen to leave "Paranormal Activity 2." In any event, he did his job, and Lionsgate leaned heavily on the ending of it all as well as the 3D gimmick in the marketing. They had to do something because critics were very much not on the movie\'s side. "Saw 3D" boasts a franchise-worst 9% critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes . That said, these movies were never critical darlings, and with a Halloween-friendly release date, as well as the promise of an ending, horror lovers showed up on opening weekend anyway. "Saw 3D" hit theaters on the weekend of October 29, 2010, topping the charts with $22.5 million. "Paranormal Activity 2" came in at number two with $16.5 million on its second weekend. Originally, the movies were set to go head-to-head . Mercifully, that didn\'t happen. Even though the movie fell off a cliff once "Megamind" and "Due Date" arrived the following weekend. It was firmly out of the top ten by its fourth weekend. It hardly mattered. The 3D gimmick worked like a charm, and the intended audience showed up in droves. It was a major rebound for the series commercially, even if it was a disaster critically. "Saw 3D" finished its run with $45.7 million domestically to go with a whopping $90.4 million internationally for a grand total of $136.1 million worldwide. Saw 3D killed the franchise — for a while anyway Lionsgate Even against a reported $17 million budget — the biggest for any of these movies up to that point — it was a huge win for the studio. The only entries that made more were "Saw III" ($164.8 million), "Saw II" ($152.9 million), and "Saw IV" ($139.3 million). All the same, Lionsgate stuck to their word and retired the franchise – for a time anyway. "If you start making movies that don\'t live up to the \'greatest hits\' in the series, it denigrates the past, and nobody wants that. We want this to go down in history as a great franchise. I think it is the last Saw movie," Greutert said to EW at the time. "But it\'s absolutely my last Saw movie." It wasn\'t the last "Saw" movie, nor was it Greutert\'s last "Saw" movie. Just over a year later, in December 2011, then-Lionsgate Vice Chairman Michael Burns stated , "I\'m sure, someday, you\'ll see \'Saw\' back in the picture." That day eventually came, albeit several years later, with "Jigsaw" in 2017. It once again fudged with the timeline so that Bell could return as John Kramer once more. It was a welcome return, bringing in over $104 million globally. The series then took a turn with the spin-off, "Spiral: From the Book of Saw." It made just $40 million. Then, Lionsgate got the band back together with Greutert returning to direct 2023\'s "Saw X," which was met with the best reviews for any movie in the series . Taking place between the events of the first two movies, it allowed for a back-to-basics approach that audiences ate up to the tune of $125.3 million worldwide. The lessons contained within Lionsgate What\'s true is that "Saw" is now a $1.1 billion franchise with a massive global footprint that includes escape rooms, theme park attractions, tons of merchandise, and more. It\'s also true that "Saw 3D" was a creative low point that got in on the right trend at the right time, positioning itself to capitalize despite its miserable reception. Case in point, per Variety , 3D ticket sales accounted for a staggering 92% of the movie\'s opening. Save for some memorable kills , the film remains largely maligned to this day. The big lesson here is that a gimmick only gets you so far. What Greutert proved with both "Saw VI" and "Saw X" is that, when motivated to be there, he is amongst the best directors to ever put John Kramer on the silver screen. When forced to be there? That\'s a different story. It\'s hard to imagine any creative person giving their best under a situation like this. It\'s in many ways not surprising that the movie didn\'t turn out. As the " Saw" franchise rights at now with Blumhouse as "Saw 11," as planned, was scrapped , the franchise\'s new owners would do well to learn from the sins of the past. The only reason an 11th "Saw" movie should exist is if someone has a good creative reason to bring it into existence. Forcing something for purely commercial reasons is a fast-burning fuel with a tank that runs out rapidly. If longevity is the key, a franchise can\'t suffer too many misfires as rough as "Saw 3D." Horror fans have been eating well this last decade on streaming television, with a lot of horror hits coming out on Netflix, HBO, and Amazon Prime Video. HBO Max, in particular, has been bringing the scares . The Last of Us , True Blood , The Outsider , and now It: Welcome to Derry are all massively popular TV shows and great examples of how to do long-form horror. Lovecraft Country should be added to this list as well. Lovecraft Country Is A Horrifying, Entertaining Series Lovecraft Country is a wildly unique horror series, and while it does include some of the mind-melting beasts courtesy of the show\'s namesake, like shoggoths and Cthulu, it\'s not an adaptation of any one H.P. story. Instead, it\'s an adaptation of Matt Ruff\'s 2016 horror novel. The series is set in 1950s Jim Crow America and follows Tic Freeman (Jonathan Majors) and Leti Lewis (Jurnee Smollett) as they embark on a dangerous road trip through some of the most racist parts of the country. They meet horrors beyond their comprehension, and bring them back to Chicago with them. While the monsters, witches, and ghosts are plenty terrifying, it\'s the violent racism they face day in and day out that puts them most at peril. Lovecraft Country is a beautifully directed show with fantastical ideas mixed in elegantly with the issues of segregation and prejudice, making for a terrifying and thoughtful experiment. Lovecraft Country Was Canceled After One Season Despite Great Reviews Lovecraft Country ran for 10 episodes, and it felt like the series had plenty of ideas for more seasons to come, but in July 2021, HBO announced that they were canceling the series (via Deadline ). HBO simply said, " We will not be moving forward with a second season of Lovecraft Country ." While Lovecraft Country season 1 had a book to go off, showrunner Misha Green and her team had to craft an original story for season 2. It sounds like HBO gave Green and her team some time to think up a new season, but ultimately decided that they would be canceling the show instead. Lovecraft Country was slow to grow, but once it did, it had significant viewing numbers. The season finale hit a viewership high with 1.5 M, becoming the most-watched new episode of an HBO Max original series in its first day. article Share this article on Talk Rita Ora led with rope ties and leather buckles at Chateau Marmont on Friday evening, wearing Zimmermann ’s Orla Buckle Sandal 85 with a coordinated resort 2026 set for the label’s collection celebration. Rita Ora wearing Zimmermann ’s Orla Buckle Sandals as she joins in on the celebration for the brand’s resort 2026 collection at Chateau Marmont on Friday in Los Angeles. Getty Images for Zimmermann The sandal, which retails for $975, is set with four straps that buckle across the foot and ankle. The smooth calf leather sandal has a rounded toe, and the 85mm cone heel forms a distinct angled line. Ora opted for the Moss iteration, a muted brown with a soft green undertone. A closer look at Rita Ora’s Zimmerman Orla Buckle Sandals . Getty Images for Zimmermann Ora paired the sandal with a two-piece white set, also from Zimmermann’s resort 2026 collection, that featured rope ties at the neck and waist. The top used knotted halter straps and wide gathered panels through the sleeves and bodice. A matching skirt continued the construction with cinched pleating and rope that crossed the torso before looping through the upper skirt seam. In late September, she reached for Gianvito Rossi kitten heels while promoting “All Natural,” pairing the pointed profile with sheer socks and a trenchcoat. A week later in Paris, she wore Giuseppe Zanotti’s Sylvy platforms at the Balenciaga Dinner — a patent style with a covered block heel and rounded platform. Earlier this month in London, she shifted to satin with Russell & Bromley’s Hillcliffe slingbacks for the Music Industry Trust Awards. Zimmermann Orla Buckle Sandal in Moss, $975. But it had been a while since Nicky and Simone Zimmermann had dropped into Los Angeles, where they opened their first-ever Stateside boutique back in 2011. (There are now some 92 standalone stores scattered across the globe.) Arriving to some very un-SoCal-like rain and flash flood warnings, the intense weather didn’t dampen the sisters’ perennially upbeat Aussie nature. Indeed, the bizarre conditions made for even more of a surreal and cinematic night at the fabled Chateau Marmont to celebrate the Twisted Romance-themed Cruise 2026 collection. Although rainwater was practically ricocheting off the neon sign erected poolside as a step-and-repeat photo moment, it didn’t deter guests from pulling their best blue steel poses, showing off their outfits for awaiting DJ-turned-photographer Myles Hendrik. As such, the best accessory of the evening proved to be a personal umbrella-wielding gentleman, ensuring no one slid right off the soaking wet tree-lined pathways. Once dried off indoors, attendees warmed up in glow of the Chateau’s candlelit bungalow over dirty martinis, glasses of Champagne, and deep belly laughter. Model Abby Champion, who has walked countless Zimmermann runways and recently wore a custom dress by Nicky Zimmermann during her wedding weekend , reunited with the Sydney-based designer. Longtime friends Emma Roberts, Dakota Fanning, and Zoey Deutch giggled together in a corner, while Jurnee Smollett introduced Halle Bailey to her older sister, Jazz. A long and languorous dinner unfolded at ethereal tables that nodded to the Twisted Romance mood. Ivory linens were laden with candelabras, deep burgundy-hued calla lilies, old silver coins, strings of pearls, and vintage glassware: an aesthetically-pleasing backdrop for crowd-favorite dishes like spicy tuna tartare, beetroot salad, Mediterranean branzino, and roasted chicken. “Tonight is about reconnecting with you all,” Nicky said, fresh from Paris where she splits her time to oversee the design atelier. “We haven't been going through LA as much as we used to, and we're lucky we get to see a lot of you around the world. Our first store in the US was on Robertson, which, like many things in our lives, came to us by chance and luck. We’ve now been in business nearly 35 years—which feels like a miracle! There’s a lot of stylists here, and we want you to know that your support is so meaningful and it has contributed a huge amount. We have always found LA, in particular, to be so supportive of us.” As anyone who owns a Zimmermann frock will tell you, they’re not pieces made for just sitting idle in. Before the last dinner fork had even hit the scallop-edged plate, guests were starting to make their way through the hotel to Penthouse 64 where the promise of dancing awaited. A corseted and ruffle-adorned Kitty Cash was already manning the DJ decks, and antique silver trays of espresso martinis were easily finding their way into outstretched hands. Actress Maria Bakalova was so relaxed, she was yapping cross-legged on the floor beside the fireplace, while the terrace became the place to grab both a chocolate madeline and a Vogue cigarette. With the rain pelting down on Sunset Boulevard and the wide open possibility of a Friday night ahead, there was simply no good reason to leave. Word travels fast too, as certain A listers who had been staying at the hotel for the GQ Men of the Year bash the night previous, caught wind and stopped by to hangout until well after 2 a.m. “I had no idea the Zimmermanns were this fun,” Rita Ora could be heard remarking. “It makes me love the clothes even more now.” Photo by: Myles Hendrik 1/18 Rita Ora Photo by: Myles Hendrik 2/18 Abby Champion, Larsen Thompson, Chloe East Photo by: Myles Hendrik 3/18 Beatrice Grannò Photo by: Myles Hendrik 4/18 Zoey Deutch, Dakota Fanning Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images 5/18 Emma Roberts More from Vogue Kate Middleton’s Dazzling Chandelier Earrings Are Steeped in Royal History Gather ’Round! Source: Getty Vogue World: Hollywood was a flex for the magazine and a long-overdue recognition of the influence film has on fashion. Also, Swarovski’s must-see “Masters of Light: Hollywood” exhibition of fashion and costume is on display and open to the public until Nov. 3. Greta Lee walks the runway during Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty Vogue World: Hollywood Is a Rah-Rah for the Fashion and Film Industries With Paramount Studios serving as a runway stage, Baz Luhrmann directing, a Chanel-clad Nicole Kidman starring, and a stacked celebrity cast and front row, Vogue World: Hollywood was a joyous mashup of fashion and film, featuring iconic Hollywood costumes, characters, fresh-off-the-runway fashion and archival looks. Say what you will about it being a pointless marketing exercise, and many online have said exactly that, but it was a rah-rah for both struggling industries, and a flex for Vogue, which is the only brand on the planet that could have pulled in all that star power. It also raised $4.5 million for the Entertainment Community Fund, providing a safety net for arts workers hit particularly hard this year. Sunday’s event brought 400-plus guests to the Paramount lot, including what were surely the most famous extras in history. “Picture’s up, places please, picture’s up!” a stage manager called over the bullhorn as they arrived on set. Miley Cyrus, Hailey Bieber and Anthony Vaccarello attend Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty “They’re stressing everybody out because we all actually do this and when you say picture’s up it’s serious!” Miley Cyrus said, walking in incognito wearing a Saint Laurent leather trench, newsboy cap and sunglasses. “I’m looking for the next motion picture star!” stylist Brad Goreski joked, looking every bit the studio boss in a dapper suit, sunglasses and slicked-back hair, arriving with Ashley Park in a corseted Wiederhoeft dress that carried a sense of costume. Brad Goreski and Ashley Park attend Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty Stars from music (Rita Ora, V, Machine Gun Kelly, Lizzo), film (Dakota Johnson, Gwyneth Paltrow, Cynthia Erivo, Taika Waititi), costume (Sandy Powell, Ruth E. Carter, Colleen Atwood), fashion (Anthony Vaccarello, Zac Posen, Jerry Lorenzo) and other power players in Anna Wintour’s orbit (Gov. Gavin Newsom, Bryan Lourd, Tyler Perry, Casey Wasserman) strolled past props, costume rails and spotlights on their way to director’s chair seats. The runway was high-energy and fast — people were having fun! — which is something we need more of in fashion and worked well for the 35-minute livestream of the show. While it was confusing to figure out what was designer-made and what was costume, that may have been the point. Damson Idris and Angela Bassett walk the runway at Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty The art forms have blurred. Costume designers have dipped their toes into fashion design and collaborated with luxury brands on films, not to mention continually influencing runway and street style decade after decade. Meanwhile, fashion designers are casting Hollywood faces as brand ambassadors, bringing even more showmanship to their runway shows and clothing to reach digital audiences, and even stepping into producing and costuming Hollywood films. All of it was on display on the runway. L.A.-based designers Kate and Laura Mulleavy were working in both worlds long before Anthony Vaccarello and Saint Laurent Films began producing awards-contending movies. They designed costumes for the 2010 film “Black Swan,” have cited the influence of films including “Suspiria” and “Star Wars” on many of their runway collections over the years, and made their own 2017 feature film, “Woodshock.” So it was fitting that several of their looks appeared on the Vogue World runway. Kendall Jenner wears a costume from “Moulin Rouge!,” a model wears a dress by Rodarte, Doja Cat wears a costume by Michael Schmidt inspired by Tina Turner in “Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome.” Source: Getty There used to be more of an impervious line between Hollywood costume and fashion; costume was for character building and serving a script, fashion was purely commercial. But all that’s gone out the window, as the relationship between Hollywood and fashion has become symbiotic. “In this era, people are able to step out of the boxes more and interact in the two fields simultaneously, and it’s accepted and celebrated,” Laura Mulleavy told me, noting that it was another polymath, Shirley Kurata, their longtime runway stylist and the costume designer for the 2022 film “Everything Everywhere All At Once,” who curated the evening’s contemporary character costumes. Jeff Goldblum walks the runway wearing Gucci at Vogue World. Source: Getty This recognition of costume designers’ contributions to visual culture — and to fashion, including countless collection mood boards — was long overdue. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve previewed a collection with a fashion designer who talks about being inspired by a particular film without naming, or even knowing, the costume designer. Hopefully, that mindset will start to change. The photo below says it all about the flow of creativity and reference from one world to the other — Wintour poses with costume designer Mona May and her iconic yellow plaid suit, as worn by Alicia Silverstone in the 1995 film “Clueless,” alongside a checked suit in the same spirit by fashion designer Thom Browne. Left to right, a model wears Thom Browne, costume designer Mona May, Condé Nast Chief Content Director Anna Wintour and a Mona May-designed costume from Clueless. Source: Getty There was a lot to look at on the runway. Some of the highlights: Kendall Jenner as a “Moulin Rouge!” showgirl in a leggy look from costume designer Catherine Martin, and “Great Gatsby” flappers — including Elizabeth Debicki — wearing beaded gowns Martin created for the 2013 film in collaboration with Prada. The tribute to the late, great style icon Diane Keaton and her influential “Annie Hall” look was not only touching but telling of how costume and fashion can intersect. It was originally developed by Keaton in 1977 with costume designer Ruth Morley, using some pieces from her personal wardrobe and some from Ralph Lauren, who recreated the look for the runway here, and has referenced it many times in his fashion collections over the years. There were also homages to the unforgettable costumes of “The Royal Tenenbaums” (Karen Patch), “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” (Arianne Phillips) and “Edward Scissorhands” (Colleen Atwood). Elizabeth Debicki wallks the runway at Vogue World. Source: Getty Angela Bassett closed the Afrofuturism section looking regal in her Ruth E. Carter gown on the heels of dancing “Black Panther” Wakandan warriors. Greta Lee worked a theatrical look and tricorne hat from fashion/costume designer Jonathan Anderson’s first Dior collection shown just weeks ago. Jeff Goldblum owned his Gucci sequin jacket and his runway walk, and Julia Garner skipped down the runway as the picture of baroque frivolity in a Milena Canonero for “Marie Antoinette” costume. Julia Garner walks the runway at Vogue World. Source: Getty Gracie Abrams played the part of Chanel ambassador, performing in a fresh-off-the-runway look by Matthieu Blazy, while Doja Cat shook her hips in a chainmail dress inspired by Tina Turner in “Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome,” but executed by L.A.’s Michael Schmidt, a too-often unsung hero of costume design and fabrication. It was a blast and nobody wanted it to end. On the way out, I ran into “Frankenstein” costume designer Kate Hawley, whose ravishing work, including curating Tiffany & Co. archival jewels and custom pieces for the film, is proof that the love affair between costume and fashion isn’t ending anytime soon. Costume designers Mona May, Sandy Powell, Catherine Martin, Ruth E. Carter, Arianne Phillips, Milena Canonero, Jacqueline West, Shirley Kurata with Anna Wintour at Vogue World: Hollywood. Source: Getty Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood” Source: Swarovski Fashion’s FYC Season Brands have descended on L.A. in what I’m calling fashion’s FYC (For Your Consideration) period in the lead-up to awards season. Everything from Boucheron jewels and hot-off-the-runway Versace to designer Camilla Franks’ fun, rock ’n’ roll resortwear and Le Monde Beryl’s red-carpet-ready silk pumps is being showcased for celebrities and stylists at spectacular events, rented hotel rooms and showrooms across the city. The goal? To create media moments, build relationships and make deals as opportunities to dress up, ramp up over the next few months. Swarovski joined the chorus Tuesday, asserting its role as chief embellisher of fashion and film. Global creative director Giovanna Engelbert and CEO Alexis Nasard hosted the opening of the Swarovski “Masters of Light” immersive exhibition — following stops in Vienna, Milan, Shanghai and Seoul — curated by Alexander Fury with a Hollywood focus for this edition. Unlike most fashion happenings, this is open to the public, through Nov. 3 in the former Amoeba Music space. Jean-Louis and Bob Mackie designed gown worn by Marilyn Monroe on display at Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood.” Source: Swarovski Cher, Viola Davis, Kylie Jenner, Elizabeth Olsen, Jeff Goldblum and many more turned out for the sparkly opening, exploring galleries showcasing Swarovski’s 130 year history of bedazzling fashion, jewelry, home decor and more. The brand has a century-long history in Hollywood, from lighting up Dorothy’s ruby red slippers in “The Wizard of Oz” (there’s a pair in the exhibition), to creating the jewels worn by Marilyn Monroe in “Gentlemen Prefer Blondes” (also here), to partnering with the Academy Awards, and on many a costume and red carpet dress. Like Vogue World, the exhibition is a conversation between fashion and costume — and full of eye candy — including the Jean-Louis and Bob Mackie-designed nude illusion dress worn by Monroe when she sang “Happy Birthday” to President John F. Kennedy, and by Kim Kardashian to the Met Gala, which had its own velvet-roped vestibule. Critics Choice Super Awards to Air This Weekend Sammi Turano November 12, 2025 Originally posted on January 6, 2021 @ 5:00 pm The Critics Choice Association (CCA) announced today the incredible line-up of talent that will join hosts Kevin Smith and Dani Fernandez at the inaugural Critics Choice Super Awards , helping them to honor the most popular, fan-obsessed genres across both television and movies, including Superhero/Comic Book, Science Fiction/Fantasy, Horror, Action and Animation. Shohreh Aghdashloo, Aya Cash, Madelyn Cline, Mike Colter, Colman Domingo, Tom Ellis, Courtney Ford, Tiffany Haddish, Sam Heughan, Maddison Jaizani, Lennie James, Martin Kove, Javicia Leslie, Leah Lewis, Caity Lotz, Ralph Macchio, Kennedy McMann, Elizabeth Mitchell, Lindsey Morgan, Bob Morley, Genevieve Padalecki, Jared Padalecki, Brandon Routh, Chase Stokes, Eliza Taylor, Gina Torres, Alan Tudyk, and William Zabka, will all serve as presenters during the special ceremony, which will air on The CW Network on Sunday, January 10, 2021 (8:00-10:00pm ET/PT) and will stream the next day for free on The CW App and cwtv.com. “We know that the Super Awards are in the best hands with Kevin Smith and Dani Fernandez at the helm,” said Critics Choice Association CEO Joey Berlin. “They bring with them an unparalleled knowledge of and enthusiasm for these sometimes underappreciated genres that we know fans and viewers will love. They are joined by a stellar line-up of fan favorites who will be on hand to support their ‘Super’ colleagues and help showcase the very best in popular entertainment.” The Critics Choice Association will also present the Legacy Award to the “Star Trek” franchise, recognizing the cultural impact it has had across multiple decades while continuing to appeal to and grow its loyal fanbase with new stories and characters. “Star Trek” icon Patrick Stewart , and “Star Trek: Discovery” trailblazer Sonequa Martin-Green will personally accept this special honor, which comes as the franchise celebrates its 55 th anniversary. See also Critics Choice Association to Honor Harrison Ford Hulu and NEON’s “Palm Springs” leads this year’s film nominees, with a total of five including Best Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Andy Samberg, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie and Best Villain in a Movie for J.K. Simmons, and Best Actress in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Cristin Milioti. Several films followed close behind with four nominations including “Birds of Prey” (Warner Bros.), “Freaky” (Universal), “Onward” (Disney+), “Sonic the Hedgehog” (Paramount), “The Hunt” (Universal), “The Old Guard” (Netflix), and “The Willoughbys” (Netflix). “Lovecraft Country” (HBO) received the most television nominations, with a total of six possible wins, including Best Horror Series, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Jonathan Majors, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Michael K. Williams, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Wunmi Mosaku, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Jurnee Smollett, and Best Villain in a Series for Abbey Lee. Amazon’s “The Boys” received five nominations including Best Superhero/Comic Book Series, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series and Best Villain in a Series for Antony Starr, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Karl Urban, and Best Actress in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Aya Cash. For the full list of nominees, and additional information, visit: https://www.criticschoice.com/critics-choice-super-awards/ Kevin Smith has been saying silly cinematic shit since 1994’s “Clerks.” 2021 marks the 27 th year since the last time he had a real job. A polygamist, he’s married to both his wife, Jen, and podcasting. Writer, comedian, and actress Dani Fernandez is a frequent speaker at San Diego Comic Con, LA Comic Con, and New York Comic Con and has been a panelist for The CW’s “Crisis Aftermath.” She has hosted for E!, Disney, Nerdist, Skybound, Funimation, and iHeartRadio, among others. She can currently be seen on Syfy’s “The Great Debate” and in Disney’s “Ralph Breaks the Internet,” playing herself. She is also an accomplished television writer with credits at Netflix and HBO Max. She pulled back her maroon Max Mara blazer to reveal a black T-shirt with the word, “resist.” Fonda continued: “I realized, given today’s reality, humanitarianism and empathy are essential forms of resistance. … It’s at the heart of what we do in our profession, empathy. And you know what else is at the heart of what we do? The First Amendment. Our profession, like all art forms, can’t exist without freedom of expression. It’s the bedrock of democracy, and it’s being taken away from us. And that’s why, on Oct. 1, we launched the Committee for the First Amendment .” Fonda clarified the Committee was re-launched, as it existed in the ’70’s and ’80s, when her father was a member. “But dig this,” she said. “That was about one small part of government robbing us of our First Amendment. Right now, it’s the entire federal government. It is far, far worse than what existed back in the ’40s and ’50s. And so, we have to do something about that.” Then she praised the recipient of this year’s Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award. “Jamie Lee Curtis and I have a few things in common,” Fonda said. “We’re both children of major movie stars and we made our own way quite successfully in their business. And we’re both late bloomers — which is okay. It moves me very deeply to see how Jamie uses her skills and her remarkable ego-less courage as an actor. … And last January, when the fires were burning and our hearts were breaking, I heard Jamie Lee Curtis had given a million dollars to the fire department and it made me cry.” Fonda added how Curtis had also raised millions of dollars for Children’s Hospital L.A., and has used her voice for addiction and trans rights. When she took the stage, Curtis also spoke about government. “I heard it today that she is retiring from public service, and I thought this Women In Film crowd could just give Nancy Pelosi a loud [round of applause]. … What an example to me of a life of service!” She also professed: “I am most excited to stand here two days after the repudiation of the authoritative regime. The election of these two beautiful women to governorships.” Curtis thanked her presenter. “Jane Fonda, I have watched you in wonder and shock and awe, at the way that you walk through the world as an artist, as an activist and as a disruptor in residence.” She noted that she joined the Committee of the First Amendment. Lastly, Kaia Gerber honored her Palm Royale co-star Kristen Wiig with the inaugural Icon Award. “Who better to receive it than my favorite scene partner?” Gerber said. “For seven years at SNL , Kristen showed us comedy could be completely unhinged and utterly ‘stupid’ — a word I learned from Kristen herself as one of the highest forms of praise in comedy — and also, somehow be simultaneously deeply human.” Kaia Gerber, Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF and Icon Award recipient Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Gerber continued, “When Bridesmaids came out, it was a revelation. … There is such truth and utter heartbreak behind [all of her characters].” She finished, “Tonight, we celebrate the woman who taught us that comedy is art, that chaos is beautiful, that sheer stupidity is not only encouraged but a necessity of life and that being unapologetically yourself might just be the most iconic move of all.” An emotional Wiig thanked Gerber, who she called “a lighthouse” on her show. “I’m fully overwhelmed,” she said. “This is my first time having to make a speech like this. I just kept thinking, ‘How did I get here?’ … I keep coming back to the people who said ‘yes’ to me before I had anything on my resume.” Wiig noted how her whole life changed when she joined The Groundlings. “That led to SNL ,” she said. She called out two men: Bridesmaids director Paul Feig and producer Judd Apatow (who reached out to her and asked if she wanted to write something). “I certainly wouldn’t be up here getting an award from Women In Film if it weren’t for that movie,” she said of the project that changed her life. Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF But ultimately, she’s enjoyed collaborating with women and exploring female characters. “I just love stories about women,” Wiig said. “We’re so crazy! We’re complex. We talk to each other about how we age, and our sensitivities and our intuition. It’s a never-ending source of material. I want to keep going,” she pledged. “I want to keep telling stories about women, with women.” Wiig then offered everyone a challenge. “I still have things in my career that I really want to do — that I’m really scared to do,” she confessed. “And so I just thought, by chance, if everyone in this room has that thing that they’ve really wanted to do or really been scared to do — maybe we make like a collective pact with each other that we’re going to just do it, anyway.” Don’t keep it to yourself…share the love! Offering game-changing shows like The Sopranos and The Wire , HBO became the creator-friendly destination that allowed original ideas to be explored with a level of quality previously unseen on network television. Some of the most important shows of the last few decades had a chance to flourish, but not all were so lucky. Whether it was due to low viewership or budgets that were impossible to sustain, a few intriguing shows couldn’t find their footing on the cable channel. These are ten canceled HBO shows that had all the potential to be great , but were unable to see their vision fully realized. For this list, we’ll only be looking at HBO originals, which will exclude any fantastic but short-lived MAX originals from making the cut. 10 \'The Nevers\' (2021) A woman in period clothing crouches down onto a road in The Nevers. Image via HBO The Nevers had an interesting premise and a talented cast and crew, but the series was unable to complete its first season. The Victorian-era series followed a group of individuals who find themselves with unique and extraordinary powers. Hunted and feared, these gifted few, known as the “touched,” must band together to operate in secret like steampunk superheroes. In an era where TV audiences are seeking new fantasy shows, The Nevers could have been the type of unique spin on the genre that developed a following . Unfortunately, the show’s creator, Joss Whedon, became persona non grata after accusations of workplace harassment from previous productions, and he would later step away from The Nevers while it was still filming. Only the first six episodes would air, and HBO canceled the series before finishing the season, a rare move for the cable channel. 9 \'The Franchise\' (2024) The production team of Maximum Studios\' "Tecto" watches their actors perform in \'The Franchise\'. Image via HBO HBO subscribers were able to peek into the fresh hell of blockbuster filmmaking with the short-lived comedy series The Franchise . The cast and crew of the superhero film Tecto: Eye of the Storm are doing their best to complete the production despite the fact that no one seems interested in the project. As daily problems besiege the set, First Assistant Director Daniel ( Himesh Patel ) is forced to find solutions to get the film wrapped. When The Franchise premiered, it was praised for its witty writing and attention to detail when satirizing the business of making superhero films. Considering the pedigree behind the camera that consisted of Jon Brown , Sam Mendes , and Armando Iannucci , expectations were high that the series would see at least a second season. Much to the disappointment of fans, The Franchise ended after one season with an open-ended finale , teeing up higher stakes and the possibility for interesting conflict that would never be realized. 8 \'Luck\' (2011–2012) Dennis Farina as Gus and Dustin Hoffman as Chester Berstein in Luck. Image via HBO A star-studded cast and a legendary television creator weren’t enough to keep Luck on track. Created by David Milch , Luck follows the many lives that intersect around the world of horse racing at a California racetrack. From the horse trainers in the stables to the gamblers who put their fates to the test, everyone has a story to tell and scores to settle on and off the track. The idea of seeing cinematic heavyweights like Dustin Hoffman and Nick Nolte chew scenery with Milch scripts was an exciting prospect. The show was critically praised, and HBO had announced a second season before later reversing the decision in light of on-set issues. Three horses had died during the production of Luck , and concern over the safety of animals led to the horse racing series finishing after only one lap. 7 \'Vinyl\' (2016) Ray Romano as Zak Yankovich in Vinyl Image via HBO Vinyl had all the makings of becoming HBO’s newest prestige hit, but the series unfortunately didn’t make it beyond one season. Set in the 1970s, Vinyl starred Bobby Cannavale as record executive Richie Finestra. Struggling to survive in a music industry beginning to change, Richie mounts a final effort to save his record label from becoming a casualty of new sounds and ideals. A show set in the music industry of the 70s offered opportunities for storylines that could have thrown the characters into real-life moments in history. However, even with names like Martin Scorsese and Mick Jagger attached as co-creators, Vinyl didn’t deliver ratings or enough critical favor to justify continuing the story . Although HBO was initially interested in producing a second season, it cut its losses after the ten episodes of season one. 6 \'Deadwood\' (2004–2007) Timothy Olyphant as Seth Bullock on \'Deadwood.\' Image via HBO It might seem strange to include a show that ran for three seasons, but Deadwood could have easily done twice that with more story left to tell. Set in the late 1800s, Deadwood brought viewers to the South Dakota gold mining camp of Deadwood. Established in a lawless territory, the residents of Deadwood searched for their fortunes before the land became an official part of the U.S. Even with only three seasons completed, Deadwood is considered by many as an essential Western show that should be watched by anyone who is a fan of the genre. Ian McShane , as the saloon owner Al Swearengen, is one of the greatest characters to appear on an HBO series, and the storylines defied what viewers expected from a typical western series. Budget concerns and a breakdown in communication between HBO and creator David Milch abruptly ended Deadwood at three seasons , but if viewers had known, at least a few would have kicked in a donation to keep the western on TV. \u200b\u200b\u200b 5 \'Lovecraft Country\' (2020) Leti stands outside in Lovecraft Country. Image via HBO For all the positive attention the series received, it’s still surprising that Lovecraft Country only produced one season. Set in the 1950s, Lovecraft Country follows Atticus ( Jonathan Majors ) as he searches for his missing father. Joining him is his friend Leticia ( Jurnee Smollett ) and his Uncle George ( Courtney B. Vance) as they encounter strange and horrific entities on their missing persons quest. HBO has experimented with many genres, but horror was mainly overlooked and limited to the anthology series Tales From the Crypt . Lovecraft Country promised to be an intelligent piece of horror that also examined relevant social issues , but the first season was also its last. Speculation regarding the cancelation varied from budgetary issues to an unclear path forward to a second season, but allegations about a toxic work environment on the Lovecraft Country set have also been mentioned regarding the unique and short-lived series. 4 \'Carnivàle\' (2003–2005) Justin stands next to a tattooed man in Carnivale. Image via HBO Carnivàle was a twisted and challenging gothic drama that failed to find an audience before its potential could be realized. Set during the Great Depression, Carnivàle told the story of two men, a runaway prisoner named Ben Hawkins ( Nick Stahl ), and a humble but conflicted Minister, Justin Crowe ( Clancy Brown ). While Justin grows his flock, Ben travels with a mystical carnival, each man destined to clash with the other in an epic showdown. Carnivàle was a narratively dense but rewarding show for those who stuck with it, constantly leaving viewers guessing as to what would happen next. Creator Daniel Knauf planned a story that would stretch over six seasons, but the dark fantasy series was cut short after two seasons. A combination of production costs and low viewership motivated HBO to make the decision, but fans will always wonder how the haunting and mysterious series would have played out under different circumstances. 3 \'Enlightened\' (2011–2013) Laura Dern as Amy with a shocked expression wearing a yellow top in \'Enlightened\' Image via HBO Fans of the dramedy Enlightened know there was a great deal of life left in the show. In Enlightened , Laura Dern stars as Amy Jellicoe, an abrasive executive who succumbs to a very public and career-damaging nervous breakdown. After returning from a wellness retreat, Amy attempts to approach her life from a calmer, more enlightened perspective, but practice proves harder than theory. Enlightened creator Mike White would later find massive success with The White Lotus , but drawing viewers to the Dern-led series proved too challenging. Although Enlightened boasted a strong performance from the ever-reliable Dern and struck a chord with the audience who tuned in, the viewing numbers were slim, even by prestige television standards . White had plans for what would happen to Amy if a third season were to take place, but Enlightened would be canceled after two seasons. 2 \'Rome\' (2005–2007) Ray Stevenson and Kevin McKidd as Roman soldiers standing alongside together in Rome (2005-2007). Image via HBO Rome was an ambitious period piece for HBO to attempt, but circumstances limited the series to a two-season run. Set in Ancient Rome, the series mixed historical events with fictional characters to give a dramatized view of Rome transitioning from a republic into an expansive empire. Rome was widely praised for its talented performances, unique approach to storytelling, and its epic scale. Truly, the word epic might be underselling it a bit, because the production quality in Rome was as if a big-budget blockbuster had been broken into episodic form for television . While the large-scale recreation of Rome was impressive, it was also expensive, and therein lay the obstacle to the show’s long-term success. A period show is already an expensive proposition, but the budget needed for Rome almost guaranteed the drama had no chance at being profitable. 1 \'Perry Mason\' (2020–2023) Matthew Rhys as Perry Mason in a suits and hat looks troubled standing outside in Perry Mason. Image via HBO In a perfect world, Perry Mason would still be churning out new seasons, but we’ll have to settle for the two we received. Before Perry Mason ( Matthew Rhys ) became a respected Defense Attorney, he was an investigator doing small-time jobs after returning from World War I. Perry is lost and looking for direction, but a sensational murder case will be the catalyst for him to embrace the next step of his career. HBO’s take on the famed fictional defense attorney was a moody, beautiful piece of noir , and Rhys’ performance was heartbreaking in its world weariness. Perry Mason was originally conceived as a miniseries, but the positive reception led to HBO picking up the drama as a regular series with a second season. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200bIn a relatively short period of time, Apple TV has established itself as a streamer with quality original programming . From the feel-good comedy Ted Lasso to the sci-fi dark mystery Severance , Apple TV covers the spectrum of tastes. The same can be said for their varied offering of crime shows. From broadly comedic whodunits to slow-burning thrillers with high stakes, Apple TV has a number of crime shows to satisfy fans of the genre. The following list covers eight of the best crime shows on Apple TV , each featuring enough murder, destruction, or robberies to keep a precinct of hardened detectives busy for the next year. 8 'Dope Thief' (2025) Brian Tyree Henry as Ray with Wagner Moura as Manny as they reel back in shock in Dope Thief. Image via Apple TV+ In Dope Thief , two friends, Ray ( Brian Tyree Henry ) and Manny ( Wagner Moura ), pose as DEA agents to rob drug houses. The plan seems like an easy enough con that won’t trace back to them, but the pair manages to draw attention from both sides of the law. In over their heads and with no one to trust, Ray and Manny will have to act carefully if they hope to survive an ordeal of their own creation. Dope Thief is beautifully shot, with cinematic visuals that make the series look more like a film than a television series. Henry and Moura’s performances are the driving force of Dope Thief , and their struggle to remain loyal to one another despite the challenges they face elevates the series past a standard crime show. Those viewers looking for a fast-paced series probably won’t find it in Dope Thief , but an audience looking for strong character work will enjoy the eight episodes. 7 'The Afterparty' (2022–2023) Ben Schwartz and Sam Richardson in The Afterparty Image via Apple TV+ The after-party of a high school reunion becomes a crime scene in the Apple murder mystery comedy The Afterparty . Pop star Xavier ( Dave Franco ) went from host to corpse in a matter of hours, and while the guests get their stories straight, the overzealous Detective Danner ( Tiffany Haddish ) sees this as a case that could make her career. Danner begins taking statements from the possible suspects, and although their stories are wildly different, a bigger picture leading to the culprit starts to form. The Afterparty is the perfect farcical murder mystery comedy ideal for fans of movies like Clue . The format of the series, where each episode is a different person’s perspective of the night’s events, avoids the trap of becoming repetitive by hiding enough clues in a story told by its reliably unreliable narrator. Each season of The Afterparty focuses on a new case with a few returning characters, but each cast is packed with comedic talent such as Sam Richardson , Zach Woods , and Ilana Glazer , making sure the improvisational-sounding flow of the comedy is consistently smooth and sharp. 6 'Smoke' (2025–Current) 'Dave Gudsen looking intently to his left in Smoke. Image via Apple TV+ Smoke follows police detective Michelle Calderone ( Jurnee Smollett ) and arson investigator Dave Gudsen ( Taron Egerton ) as they attempt to track down two serial arsonists. Gudsen balks at having Calderone assigned to his case, but soon, a mutual respect grows between the two. However, each has personal demons that factor into their investigation — demons that could likely put them on opposite sides as more details come to light. The point of view of our arsonists, the horrific damage they cause, and the enjoyment they receive from it leads to some truly creepy moments that will stick in the mind for days afterward. Egerton and Smollett play off one another well, and as their relationship continues to change over the nine episodes, we see the two investigators wordlessly switch tactics with one another, making for a compelling watch. When the plot twists in Smoke land, they drastically impact the story and guarantee the “Next Episode’ button is getting pressed. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 5 'Presumed Innocent' (2024–Current) Rusty is being led away in handcuffs in court with Raymond following in Presumed Innocent. Image via Apple TV+ The murder of an assistant prosecuting attorney becomes an even bigger scandal when the Chief Deputy Prosecutor is named the prime suspect. Presumed Innocent follows Rusty Sabich ( Jake Gyllenhaal ) as he is arrested and tried for the murder of his colleague, Carolyn Polhemus ( Renate Reinsve ), with whom he was having an affair. As the court case drags shameful secrets into the light, Rusty will find it increasingly difficult to prove his innocence. Even for those familiar with the original novel of the same name by Scott Turow or the 1990 film adaptation starring Harrison Ford , the TV version of Presumed Innocent will offer new plot twists to keep viewers engaged. Gyllenhaal shines as a man grappling with guilt about his involvement with the victim , but there’s no weak link in the phenomenal cast that includes Ruth Negga as his wife, Barbara, and Bill Camp as his former boss-turned-legal counsel, Raymond Horgan. The second season of Presumed Innocent will shift the series into an anthology format with a new case to follow, but anyone looking for a quick binge will receive a complete story with Season 1. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 4 'Bad Monkey' (2024–Current) Vince Vaughn sitting in a beach chair with a drink in Bad Monkey Episode 1. Image via Apple TV+ In Bad Monkey , Andrew Yancy ( Vince Vaughn ) was a great police detective who became a fairly apathetic health inspector after an altercation that put him in hot water. The arrival of a severed arm pulls Yancy back into some unofficial police work, and the fast-talking health inspector finds himself the target of some dangerous and increasingly desperate individuals. In the off chance Yancy can keep his personal life under control, he has a fighting chance of repairing his professional life if he can avoid getting killed in the process. Based on the novel of the same name by Carl Hiaasen, Bad Monkey allows its characters to be playful and get lost in banter while never losing sight of the murder mystery or the stakes of the case. Bad Monkey is the best balance of comedy and crime currently on Apple TV , and with a lead like Vaughn, who can keep one foot in both genres easily, it's a series that lends itself to substantial longevity on the streamer. The second season of Bad Monkey promises to give Yancy new co-stars to tangle with , which is one more reason to be excited for the return of the likable series. 3 'Your Friends & Neighbors' (2025–Current) A man goes from the envy of his upper-class community to the person breaking into their homes in Your Friends & Neighbors . Andrew “Coop” Cooper ( Jon Hamm ) is still emotionally reeling after the divorce from his wife, Mel ( Amanda Peet ), when he loses his job as a prominent hedge fund manager. Jaded from his recent failures and disillusioned by the wealth he sees around him, Coop begins to steal from the people he once thought of as friends. However, entering their homes allows Coop access to more than their valuables — he also discovers secrets they would kill to protect. Your Friends & Neighbors wisely relied on the charm and dry comedic ability of Hamm in the early stages of its story, but the series slowly built an interesting world around him. By the end of Season 1, many of the supporting characters were fully fleshed out into people who could carry side plots, which will only stand to make the show better. The end of Season 1 left many questions about how Coop moves forward with his life in light of major decisions, so it will be intriguing to see what his next steps are and how they impact his family, friends… and neighbors for Season 2. 2 'Criminal Record' (2024–Current) Cush Jumbo and Peter Capaldi standing beside each other in Criminal Record Image via Apple TV+ New details about an old murder case pit two detectives against one another in Criminal Record . An anonymous phone call leads Detective Sergeant June Lenker ( Cush Jumbo ) to believe an innocent man might be in jail for a murder he didn’t commit. June’s attempts to uncover the truth are blocked by Detective Chief Inspector Daniel Hegarty ( Peter Capaldi ), who believes firmly that the case in question should remain closed. When neither detective backs down, a professional disagreement quickly becomes personal. Criminal Record is one of Apple TV’s best crime offerings, loaded with the type of expertly laid out plot twists and tense drama that are the recipe for addictive television. Capaldi and Jumbo create a unique antagonistic chemistry that puts a fresh spin on a procedural mystery thriller, where the more they outmaneuver one another, the deeper their respect and will to succeed grow. With a confirmed second season of Criminal Record on the way, now is a great time to catch up before June and Daniel are back on the case. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 1 'Black Bird' (2022) James in on a payphone in prison in Black Bird. Image via Apple TV+ In the intense and thrilling miniseries Black Bird , Jimmy (Taron Egerton) is a small-time crook given a once-in-a-lifetime chance to commute his 10-year sentence. The prize is great, and so is the challenge: Jimmy must befriend fellow inmate Larry Hall ( Paul Walter Hauser ) with the goal of getting a confession about suspected murders. Larry is distrustful, guards are dangerous, and Jimmy doesn’t have much time before the offer expires. Egerton takes Jimmy from arrogant to honorable with no false moments, and Hauser rightfully won an Emmy by making Larry one of the most unnerving characters on television that year. There are moments of Black Bird that become so uncomfortably tense that it’s not uncommon to feel tired after watching an episode . That’s said as the highest form of compliment, because the story continues to raise the stakes scene by scene via a masterful combination of writing and acting, making Black Bird the easiest recommendation for fans of any genre.
